It uses extension methods on objects (`result.ShouldBe(...)`) rather than wrapper objects, making it easier to adopt incrementally alongside existing test code. [community]

```csharp
using Shouldly;
using Xunit;

public class OrderTotalsTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void CalculateTotal_WithDiscount_ReturnsCorrectAmount()
    {
        var order = new Order
        {
            Lines = [
                new OrderLine { UnitPrice = 100m, Quantity = 2 },
                new OrderLine { UnitPrice = 50m,  Quantity = 1 },
            ],
            DiscountPercent = 10
        };

        var total = OrderCalculator.CalculateTotal(order);

        // Shouldly produces: "total should be 225.0m but was 240.0m"
        total.ShouldBe(225.0m);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void ProcessOrders_AllPending_CompletesWithoutErrors()
    {
        var orders = Enumerable.Range(1, 5)
            .Select(i => new Order { Id = i, Status = OrderStatus.Pending })
            .ToList();

        var processor = new OrderProcessor();
        var results   = processor.Process(orders);

        results.ShouldNotBeEmpty();
        results.ShouldAllBe(r => r.Status == OrderStatus.Completed);
        results.Count.ShouldBe(5);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void FindOrder_WhenMissing_ThrowsOrderNotFoundException()
    {
        var repo = new InMemoryOrderRepository();

        // Shouldly captures the exception and shows what was thrown vs expected
        Should.Throw<OrderNotFoundException>(() => repo.FindById(999))
              .Message.ShouldContain("999");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Choose Shouldly when you want minimal-setup assertions with excellent default error messages for simple scalar, collection, and exception assertions. Do NOT choose it when you need deeply fluent collection assertions (e.g., `SatisfyRespectively`, per-element lambdas) or custom assertion extensions — FluentAssertions has significantly richer APIs for those cases. The two libraries can coexist in the same project. Alternative: FluentAssertions (broader API, richer chaining), xUnit `Assert.*` (no extra dependency, minimal messages). [community]

---

### gRPC Service Testing With `GrpcChannel` and `TestServer`

ASP.NET Core gRPC services can be integration-tested by combining `WebApplicationFactory` with a `GrpcChannel` that routes calls through `TestServer`'s in-process HTTP/2 handler. No real port is needed, so tests are fast and port-conflict-free. [official]

```csharp
using Grpc.Net.Client;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost;
using Xunit;

// Proto-generated: GreeterService, HelloRequest, HelloReply
public class GreeterServiceIntegrationTests
    : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    private readonly WebApplicationFactory<Program> _factory;

    public GreeterServiceIntegrationTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
        => _factory = factory;

    [Fact]
    public async Task SayHello_ReturnsExpectedMessage()
    {
        // Create an HttpClient that routes through TestServer
        var httpClient = _factory.CreateDefaultClient();

        // Build a GrpcChannel backed by the TestServer's handler
        var channel = GrpcChannel.ForAddress(
            httpClient.BaseAddress!,
            new GrpcChannelOptions { HttpClient = httpClient });

        var client  = new Greeter.GreeterClient(channel);
        var request = new HelloRequest { Name = "IntegrationTest" };

        var reply = await client.SayHelloAsync(request);

        Assert.Equal("Hello IntegrationTest", reply.Message);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task SayHello_WithAuthToken_ReturnsAuthorizedMessage()
    {
        var httpClient = _factory
            .WithWebHostBuilder(b => b.ConfigureTestServices(services =>
                services.AddTestAuthHandler()))
            .CreateDefaultClient();

        httpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization =
            new System.Net.Http.Headers.AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", "test-token");

        var channel = GrpcChannel.ForAddress(httpClient.BaseAddress!,
            new GrpcChannelOptions { HttpClient = httpClient });

        var client = new Greeter.GreeterClient(channel);
        var reply  = await client.SayHelloAsync(new HelloRequest { Name = "Auth" });

        Assert.Equal("Hello Auth (authorized)", reply.Message);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** This pattern provides true end-to-end gRPC integration tests (proto serialization, interceptors, auth, middleware) without network I/O. Do NOT use it to test the proto contract itself (use `protoc` linting and generated code snapshots for that). The `GrpcChannelOptions.HttpClient` property must be set — without it, gRPC falls back to real network calls, defeating in-process testing. Alternative: unit-test service implementations directly by calling the method (bypasses gRPC pipeline), WireMock.Net for external process mocking. [official]

---

### OpenTelemetry — Asserting Traces in Tests With `InMemoryExporter`

The `OpenTelemetry.Exporter.InMemory` NuGet package provides a `List<Activity>`-based exporter for asserting that your instrumentation emits the expected traces in unit and integration tests. No Jaeger, Zipkin, or OTLP endpoint required. [official]

```csharp
using System.Diagnostics;
using OpenTelemetry;
using OpenTelemetry.Trace;
using Xunit;

public class TelemetryAssertionTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void PlaceOrder_EmitsExpectedSpan()
    {
        // Arrange: capture exported activities in-memory
        var exportedActivities = new List<Activity>();
        using var tracerProvider = Sdk.CreateTracerProviderBuilder()
            .AddSource("MyApp.OrderService")
            .AddInMemoryExporter(exportedActivities)
            .Build();

        var repo    = new Mock<IOrderRepository>();
        var service = new OrderService(repo.Object);

        // Act
        service.PlaceOrder(new Order { Id = 1 });

        // Assert
        var span = exportedActivities
            .SingleOrDefault(a => a.DisplayName == "PlaceOrder");

        Assert.NotNull(span);
        Assert.Equal(ActivityStatusCode.Ok, span.Status);
        Assert.Equal("1", span.GetTagItem("order.id")?.ToString());
    }

    [Fact]
    public void PlaceOrder_WhenInvalid_EmitsErrorSpan()
    {
        var exportedActivities = new List<Activity>();
        using var tracerProvider = Sdk.CreateTracerProviderBuilder()
            .AddSource("MyApp.OrderService")
            .AddInMemoryExporter(exportedActivities)
            .Build();

        var service = new OrderService(new Mock<IOrderRepository>().Object);

        Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() =>
            service.PlaceOrder(new Order { Id = -1 }));

        var span = exportedActivities.Single(a => a.DisplayName == "PlaceOrder");
        Assert.Equal(ActivityStatusCode.Error, span.Status);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Add in-memory telemetry assertions to integration tests for critical observability paths (payment flows, auth events) to prevent silent instrumentation regressions. Do NOT assert telemetry in every unit test — the overhead of configuring `TracerProvider` per test adds noise. Keep telemetry assertions in a dedicated `Observability` test class. Alternative: `ActivityListener` directly on `ActivitySource` (lower-level, no extra NuGet), `MetricCollector<T>` from `Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.Testing` for metrics. [official]

---

### Stryker.NET — Mutation Testing to Measure Test Suite Quality

Stryker.NET mutates your source code (changes `+` to `-`, flips `>` to `>=`, nullifies return values) and then runs your test suite against each mutant. A mutant that is NOT caught by any test is a "survived mutant" — evidence that your tests lack coverage of that logical branch. [community]

```csharp
// Example: source under test with a subtle boundary condition
public class AgeValidator
{
    // Stryker will mutate `>= 18` to `> 18` — your tests must catch this
    public bool IsAdult(int age) => age >= 18;
}

// Adequate test suite — kills both >= and > mutations:
public class AgeValidatorTests
{
    [Theory]
    [InlineData(17, false)]   // below boundary — kills > mutation
    [InlineData(18, true)]    // on boundary   — kills >= vs > mutation
    [InlineData(19, true)]    // above boundary
    public void IsAdult_ReturnsExpectedResult(int age, bool expected)
    {
        var validator = new AgeValidator();
        Assert.Equal(expected, validator.IsAdult(age));
    }
}

// Run Stryker from the test project directory:
//   dotnet stryker --threshold-break 80 --threshold-high 90
//
// stryker-config.json (recommended for CI):
// {
//   "stryker-config": {
//     "project": "MyApp.csproj",
//     "threshold-break": 80,
//     "reporters": ["html", "json"],
//     "ignore-mutations": ["string", "Linq.ElementAt"]
//   }
// }
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Run Stryker on the most critical domain logic modules (pricing, authorization, validation) to expose gaps in test logic coverage that line coverage misses. Do NOT run Stryker across the entire solution on every CI commit — a full mutation run can take 10–60 minutes. Schedule it as a nightly job or run it manually before merging critical PRs. Alternative: PIT (Java-only), manual branch coverage review, property-based testing with FsCheck (catches boundary conditions through generation). [community]

---

### Alba — ASP.NET Core Integration Testing DSL

Alba is a `WebApplicationFactory`-based test DSL that wraps HTTP request/response in a fluent scenario API, reducing integration test boilerplate to a handful of lines. It is particularly ergonomic for testing JSON APIs and OpenAPI contract compliance. [community]

```csharp
using Alba;
using Xunit;

public class ProductApiAlbaTests : IAsyncLifetime
{
    private IAlbaHost _host = null!;

    public async Task InitializeAsync()
    {
        // AlbaHost wraps WebApplicationFactory internally
        _host = await AlbaHost.For<Program>(builder =>
        {
            builder.ConfigureServices(services =>
                services.AddSingleton<IProductRepository, FakeProductRepository>());
        });
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task GetProduct_WhenExists_Returns200WithBody()
    {
        // Scenario DSL: build request + assert response in one block
        await _host.Scenario(scenario =>
        {
            scenario.Get.Url("/api/products/1");
            scenario.StatusCodeShouldBe(200);
            scenario.ContentTypeShouldBe("application/json; charset=utf-8");
        });
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task CreateProduct_WithValidBody_Returns201()
    {
        var newProduct = new { Name = "Widget", Price = 9.99 };

        var result = await _host.Scenario(scenario =>
        {
            scenario.Post.Json(newProduct).ToUrl("/api/products");
            scenario.StatusCodeShouldBe(201);
        });

        var created = await result.ReadAsJsonAsync<ProductDto>();
        Assert.NotNull(created?.Id);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task GetProduct_WhenMissing_Returns404()
    {
        await _host.Scenario(scenario =>
        {
            scenario.Get.Url("/api/products/99999");
            scenario.StatusCodeShouldBe(404);
        });
    }

    public async Task DisposeAsync() => await _host.DisposeAsync();
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use Alba when your integration test suite has many HTTP scenarios that share the same host setup — the DSL eliminates the `HttpClient.GetAsync`, `response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode`, `response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync` ceremony. Do NOT use it if you need fine-grained control over `HttpRequestMessage` construction (custom headers, multipart, streaming) — drop down to `WebApplicationFactory.CreateClient()` directly. Alba targets JSON/REST APIs; it has limited support for Razor pages and Blazor server. Alternative: `WebApplicationFactory` + `HttpClient` (more control, more boilerplate), `TestServer.CreateRequest` (lower-level). [community]

---

### xUnit v3 — `ITestContextAccessor` for Infrastructure Libraries

xUnit v3's `ITestContextAccessor` is a DI-injectable interface that exposes `TestContext.Current` without requiring a static call. This is the correct pattern for test infrastructure libraries (logging adapters, fixture helpers) that need to read the current test context without becoming coupled to a static property. [official]

```csharp
using Xunit;
using Xunit.v3;

// Infrastructure adapter: labels log entries with the current test name
public class TestNamedLogger(ITestContextAccessor contextAccessor, ILogger inner)
    : ILogger
{
    public void Log<TState>(LogLevel logLevel, EventId eventId,
        TState state, Exception? exception,
        Func<TState, Exception?, string> formatter)
    {
        var testName = contextAccessor.Current?.Test.TestDisplayName ?? "unknown";
        var message  = $"[{testName}] {formatter(state, exception)}";
        inner.Log(logLevel, eventId, state, exception, (_, _) => message);
    }

    public bool IsEnabled(LogLevel logLevel) => inner.IsEnabled(logLevel);

    public IDisposable? BeginScope<TState>(TState state) where TState : notnull
        => inner.BeginScope(state);
}

// Registration in a test fixture
public class LoggingFixture
{
    public ILogger CreateLogger(ITestContextAccessor contextAccessor)
        => new TestNamedLogger(contextAccessor, new ConsoleLogger());
}

// Usage in a test class
public class PaymentServiceTests(ITestContextAccessor contextAccessor)
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task ProcessPayment_LogsSuccessEvent()
    {
        var logger  = new LoggingFixture().CreateLogger(contextAccessor);
        var service = new PaymentService(logger);

        await service.ProcessAsync(new Payment { Amount = 100m });

        // Log entries will be prefixed with the test display name
        Assert.True(true); // real assertion on captured logs
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `ITestContextAccessor` in infrastructure libraries that need the test context but cannot use `TestContext.Current` directly (e.g., because they are tested in isolation or need DI compatibility). Do NOT use `ITestContextAccessor` in production code — it is a test-only interface with no runtime implementation. Alternative: `TestContext.Current` static property (simpler when DI is not a concern), `ITestOutputHelper` for pure logging scenarios. [official]

---

### NUnit — `Assert.That` With `Throws.InstanceOf<T>` for Exception Hierarchy Assertions

NUnit's constraint-based `Assert.That(() => ..., Throws.InstanceOf<T>())` checks that the thrown exception is an instance of `T` or any subclass — unlike `Throws.TypeOf<T>()` which requires an exact type match. This is the correct pattern when asserting against abstract exception hierarchies. [official]

```csharp
using NUnit.Framework;

[TestFixture]
public class PaymentGatewayExceptionTests
{
    private PaymentGateway _gateway = null!;

    [SetUp]
    public void SetUp() => _gateway = new PaymentGateway(new StubPaymentProvider());

    [Test]
    public void ProcessPayment_WhenNetworkError_ThrowsTransientException()
    {
        // Throws.InstanceOf<T> matches PaymentTransientException AND any subclass
        Assert.That(
            () => _gateway.ProcessPayment(new Payment { Amount = -1m }),
            Throws.InstanceOf<PaymentException>());
    }

    [Test]
    public void ProcessPayment_WhenCardDeclined_ThrowsDeclinedException_WithCode()
    {
        var ex = Assert.Throws<CardDeclinedException>(
            () => _gateway.ProcessPayment(new Payment { Amount = 999999m }));

        Assert.That(ex,                Is.Not.Null);
        Assert.That(ex!.DeclineCode,   Is.EqualTo("INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS"));
        Assert.That(ex.Message,        Does.Contain("declined"));
    }

    [Test]
    public void ProcessPayment_WhenAmountIsZero_DoesNotThrow()
    {
        // Explicit assertion that no exception is thrown
        Assert.That(
            () => _gateway.ProcessPayment(new Payment { Amount = 0m }),
            Throws.Nothing);
    }

    [Test]
    public void ProcessPayment_WhenAmountNegative_ThrowsArgumentException_WithParamName()
    {
        var ex = Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(
            () => _gateway.ProcessPayment(new Payment { Amount = -1m }));

        Assert.That(ex!.ParamName, Is.EqualTo("amount"));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Prefer `Throws.InstanceOf<T>` over `Throws.TypeOf<T>` when your exception hierarchy uses subclasses for specificity (e.g., `NetworkTimeoutException : PaymentTransientException`). Use `Throws.TypeOf<T>` only when you intentionally need an exact-type assertion (e.g., ensuring a factory never wraps exceptions). Do NOT mix `Assert.Throws<T>` and `Throws.InstanceOf<T>` in the same fixture — choose one style consistently. Alternative: xUnit `Assert.Throws<T>` + `is` pattern matching for hierarchy, FluentAssertions `Should().Throw<T>()`. [official]

---

### MSTest v3 — Constructor + `IAsyncDisposable` Replaces `[TestInitialize]` / `[TestCleanup]`

MSTest v3 supports class constructors and `IAsyncDisposable.DisposeAsync()` as lifecycle hooks, matching xUnit's model. This eliminates the async-void `[TestInitialize]` problem and enables injecting real dependencies from test framework infrastructure. [official]

```csharp
using Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting;
using System;
using System.Threading.Tasks;

[TestClass]
public class OrderServiceMSTestV3Tests : IAsyncDisposable
{
    private readonly Mock<IOrderRepository> _repo;
    private readonly OrderService _service;
    private readonly SqliteConnection _connection;

    // Constructor-based setup — runs before each test (MSTest v3 instantiates
    // a new class instance per test, same as xUnit)
    public OrderServiceMSTestV3Tests()
    {
        _repo       = new Mock<IOrderRepository>();
        _service    = new OrderService(_repo.Object);
        _connection = new SqliteConnection("Data Source=:memory:");
        _connection.Open();
    }

    [TestMethod]
    public async Task PlaceOrder_CallsRepositorySave()
    {
        var order = new Order { Id = 1 };
        _repo.Setup(r => r.SaveAsync(order, default)).ReturnsAsync(true);

        var result = await _service.PlaceOrderAsync(order);

        Assert.IsTrue(result);
        _repo.Verify(r => r.SaveAsync(order, default), Times.Once());
    }

    [TestMethod]
    public async Task PlaceOrder_WhenRepoThrows_PropagatesException()
    {
        _repo.Setup(r => r.SaveAsync(It.IsAny<Order>(), default))
             .ThrowsAsync(new InvalidOperationException("DB down"));

        await Assert.ThrowsExceptionAsync<InvalidOperationException>(
            () => _service.PlaceOrderAsync(new Order { Id = 2 }));
    }

    // IAsyncDisposable replaces [TestCleanup] — async teardown without async void
    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
    {
        await _connection.DisposeAsync();
        GC.SuppressFinalize(this);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Migrate `[TestInitialize]` / `[TestCleanup]` to constructor + `IAsyncDisposable` in MSTest v3 projects — it removes the async-void footgun and aligns with xUnit style. Do NOT use `[TestInitialize]` with `async void` — exceptions are unobserved and tests may appear to pass. For shared (class-level) resources, `[ClassInitialize]` and `[ClassCleanup]` still require the `static` + `async Task` signature. Alternative: xUnit `IClassFixture<T>` (explicit sharing model), NUnit `[OneTimeSetUp]` / `[SetUp]` (attribute-based, mature tooling). [official]

---

### FluentAssertions v8 — `AssertionChain` API for Custom Assertion Extensions

FluentAssertions v8 introduced the `AssertionChain` API replacing the obsolete `Execute.Assertion` chained builder. Custom assertion extensions built on the old API must be migrated to `AssertionChain.GetOrCreate()` to avoid deprecation warnings and future breaking changes. [official]

```csharp
using FluentAssertions;
using FluentAssertions.Execution;
using FluentAssertions.Primitives;
using Xunit;

// Custom assertion for a domain type
public class OrderAssertions(Order? subject)
    : ReferenceTypeAssertions<Order?, OrderAssertions>(subject)
{
    protected override string Identifier => "order";

    public AndConstraint<OrderAssertions> BeConfirmed(
        string because = "", params object[] becauseArgs)
    {
        // v8 API: AssertionChain replaces Execute.Assertion
        AssertionChain.GetOrCreate()
            .BecauseOf(because, becauseArgs)
            .ForCondition(Subject?.Status == OrderStatus.Confirmed)
            .FailWith("Expected {context:order} to be confirmed{reason}, " +
                      "but status was {0}.", Subject?.Status);

        return new AndConstraint<OrderAssertions>(this);
    }

    public AndConstraint<OrderAssertions> HaveTotal(
        decimal expected, string because = "", params object[] becauseArgs)
    {
        AssertionChain.GetOrCreate()
            .BecauseOf(because, becauseArgs)
            .ForCondition(Subject?.Total == expected)
            .FailWith("Expected order total to be {0}{reason}, but found {1}.",
                expected, Subject?.Total);

        return new AndConstraint<OrderAssertions>(this);
    }
}

public static class OrderAssertionExtensions
{
    public static OrderAssertions Should(this Order? order) => new(order);
}

public class OrderAssertionExtensionTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void ConfirmOrder_SetsStatusAndTotal()
    {
        var order = new Order { Id = 1, Lines = [new OrderLine { UnitPrice = 50m, Quantity = 2 }] };
        order.Confirm();

        order.Should().BeConfirmed("the order was explicitly confirmed")
             .And.HaveTotal(100m, "two units at 50 each");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Build `AssertionChain`-based custom assertions for any domain type that appears frequently in tests — they encode the assertion vocabulary of the domain in one place. Do NOT build custom assertions for types with fewer than 3–5 test usages — the API has ceremony (class + extension method) that pays off only with repetition. When migrating from FA v7, run `Find All References` for `Execute.Assertion` to identify all callsites before updating. Alternative: `Shouldly` custom assertion helpers (simpler, `ShouldSatisfy`), inline xUnit `Assert` calls with local helper methods. [official]

---

### Moq — `MockBehavior.Strict` With Selective `Setup` as an Explicit Contract Test

`MockBehavior.Strict` causes any unmocked call to throw `MockException`, effectively treating the mock as an explicit interface contract test — only the calls your code is supposed to make are permitted. Combined with minimal setups, this finds unexpected side effects. [community]

```csharp
using Moq;
using Xunit;

public interface INotificationSender
{
    Task SendEmailAsync(string to, string subject, string body, CancellationToken ct);
    Task SendSmsAsync(string phoneNumber, string message, CancellationToken ct);
    Task LogAsync(string eventName, CancellationToken ct);
}

public class OrderConfirmationServiceTests
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task ConfirmOrder_SendsOnlyEmailNotification_NeverSms()
    {
        // Strict mode: any call NOT listed in Setup() throws MockException
        var sender = new Mock<INotificationSender>(MockBehavior.Strict);

        // Only allow email — SMS should never be called for order confirmations
        sender.Setup(s =>
            s.SendEmailAsync(
                "customer@example.com",
                It.Is<string>(subj => subj.Contains("Confirmed")),
                It.IsAny<string>(),
                It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()))
            .Returns(Task.CompletedTask);

        var service = new OrderConfirmationService(sender.Object);
        await service.ConfirmAsync(new Order
        {
            Id = 1, CustomerEmail = "customer@example.com"
        });

        // No explicit Verify needed — Strict mode enforced that SendSmsAsync was not called
        sender.VerifyAll(); // verify all Setup() calls were actually made
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `MockBehavior.Strict` for core domain service tests where unexpected dependency calls indicate a logic error (e.g., a service that should ONLY send email must not silently send SMS). Do NOT use Strict mode across all tests — it makes tests brittle when the production API grows (every new method requires a `Setup`). Reserve it for high-stakes contracts. Alternative: `MockBehavior.Loose` + explicit `VerifyNoOtherCalls()` (same guarantees, less friction on API growth), NSubstitute (throws by default on unset calls). [community]

---

### `WireMock.Net` — HTTP Dependency Stubbing for Integration Tests

WireMock.Net starts an in-process HTTP server that matches incoming requests against declarative stub rules and returns configured responses. Use it to stub third-party REST APIs (Stripe, Twilio, external services) in integration tests without needing test doubles in production code. [community]

```csharp
using WireMock.RequestBuilders;
using WireMock.ResponseBuilders;
using WireMock.Server;
using Xunit;

public class PaymentGatewayClientTests : IDisposable
{
    private readonly WireMockServer _server;
    private readonly HttpClient     _httpClient;

    public PaymentGatewayClientTests()
    {
        _server = WireMockServer.Start(); // random port — no conflicts

        // Stub POST /v1/charges → 200 with a Stripe-like response body
        _server
            .Given(Request.Create()
                .WithPath("/v1/charges")
                .WithHeader("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_*")
                .UsingPost())
            .RespondWith(Response.Create()
                .WithStatusCode(200)
                .WithHeader("Content-Type", "application/json")
                .WithBodyAsJson(new { id = "ch_test_123", status = "succeeded" }));

        // Stub for declined card scenario
        _server
            .Given(Request.Create()
                .WithPath("/v1/charges")
                .WithBody(b => b.Contains("4000000000000002"))
                .UsingPost())
            .RespondWith(Response.Create()
                .WithStatusCode(402)
                .WithBodyAsJson(new { error = new { code = "card_declined" } }));

        _httpClient = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri(_server.Url!) };
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Charge_WithValidCard_ReturnsSucceeded()
    {
        var client = new StripePaymentGatewayClient(_httpClient);
        var result = await client.ChargeAsync(amount: 999, cardToken: "tok_visa");

        Assert.Equal("succeeded", result.Status);
        Assert.Equal("ch_test_123", result.ChargeId);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Charge_WithDeclinedCard_ThrowsPaymentDeclinedException()
    {
        var client = new StripePaymentGatewayClient(_httpClient);

        await Assert.ThrowsAsync<PaymentDeclinedException>(
            () => client.ChargeAsync(amount: 999, cardToken: "tok_4000000000000002"));
    }

    public void Dispose() => _server.Stop();
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** WireMock.Net excels at stubbing HTTP APIs that you cannot modify (third-party services), especially when you need realistic error scenarios (rate limits, 5xx, malformed responses) that are hard to trigger against real services. Do NOT use it when you can inject an `HttpMessageHandler` mock — that is lighter-weight and works without a port. WireMock starts a TCP listener, so use `WireMockServer.Start()` without a port argument for random-port assignment to avoid conflicts in parallel test runs. Alternative: `MockHttpMessageHandler` from `RichardSzalay.MockHttp` (no-port, in-process), `ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler` (already covered for named clients). [community]

---

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 30

**Testcontainers `WithReuse(true)` causes silently stale container state when migrations are not idempotent [community]** — When `WithReuse(true)` is active and the container is reused from a previous run, `InitializeAsync` is effectively a no-op (the container is already running). If your migration logic is not idempotent (e.g., `CREATE TABLE` without `IF NOT EXISTS`), the second run either throws a migration error or silently operates against a database with stale data from the prior session. WHY it causes problems: tests that assert on row counts or clean state produce false failures that only appear on the second and subsequent runs, not the first. Fix: always write idempotent migration scripts (`IF NOT EXISTS`, `TRUNCATE` in setup, or use Respawn between tests) when pairing `WithReuse(true)` with a stateful container.

**NetArchTest `Types.InCurrentDomain()` misses assemblies not yet loaded — architecture rules pass trivially as false greens [community]** — `Types.InCurrentDomain()` calls `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies()`, which only includes assemblies that have been loaded into the current process. If the target assembly is never referenced by a test class, it may not be loaded at assertion time. WHY it causes problems: an architecture rule against `MyApp.Infrastructure` passes trivially because the assembly is never scanned — the test is a false green that provides false confidence. Fix: always use `Types.InAssembly(typeof(SomeTypeFromTargetAssembly).Assembly)` to force loading of the specific assembly you want to scan.

**Stryker mutates test helper methods as well as source-under-test when `project` is not configured — mutation score is artificially penalized [community]** — If `stryker-config.json` does not specify `"project"` pointing to the source project, Stryker may include test helper classes in the mutation set. Mutants in `TestHelpers.cs` cannot be killed because no test asserts on test helper behavior directly. WHY it causes problems: the mutation score is artificially lowered by unkillable mutants, causing `--threshold-break` failures that are unrelated to real coverage gaps. Fix: always set `"project": "MyApp.csproj"` (the source project) in `stryker-config.json`, never the test project.

**WireMock.Net stubs match in registration order — later stubs for the same route silently shadow earlier ones in shared server tests [community]** — WireMock.Net evaluates stubs from most recently registered to oldest when multiple stubs match the same request. If two test methods register conflicting stubs without resetting the server, the second test's stubs shadow the first test's stubs. WHY it causes problems: tests that run in a certain order pass; when the order changes (parallel execution, test framework reordering), the wrong stub matches and assertions fail with puzzling response mismatches. Fix: call `_server.Reset()` in constructor / `[SetUp]` between tests, or use a separate `WireMockServer` instance per test class.

**gRPC `GrpcChannel.ForAddress` with a `TestServer`-backed `HttpClient` throws `RpcException` `Unavailable` when the HTTP/2 app context switch is missing [community]** — gRPC-dotnet refuses to use HTTP/1.1 for transport by default. When `TestServer` serves HTTP/1.1 (the default unless Kestrel is configured for HTTP/2), gRPC calls fail immediately with status `Unavailable` and an opaque "Connection refused" message. WHY it causes problems: the error message does not mention HTTP versions, leading developers to debug network configuration rather than protocol mismatch. Fix: set `AppContext.SetSwitch("System.Net.Http.SocketsHttpHandler.Http2UnencryptedSupport", true)` in the test assembly initializer, or configure `WebApplicationFactory` to use HTTP/2 via Kestrel `UseUrls` + `ListenAnyIP` options.

**FluentAssertions v8 `AssertionChain.GetOrCreate()` returns a shared chain per scope — calling it twice in one assertion method produces incorrect failure aggregation [community]** — `AssertionChain.GetOrCreate()` is designed to be called once per assertion method. If you call it twice and add conditions to both results, the second call returns the *same* chain instance inside `AssertionScope`. Conditions from both calls are combined, and a failure in one may suppress failure reporting for the other. WHY it causes problems: a custom assertion that chains two independent `ForCondition` calls using two `GetOrCreate()` calls may report partial success and hide one failure, producing tests that appear to pass when both conditions should fail. Fix: call `AssertionChain.GetOrCreate()` exactly once per public assertion method and chain all `.ForCondition(...).FailWith(...)` calls on that single instance.

---

### Anti-Patterns Quick Reference — Cycle 30 Additions

| Anti-Pattern | Why It's Harmful | What to Do Instead |
|---|---|---|
| Using `WithReuse(true)` with non-idempotent migrations | Second test run fails or operates against stale data | Use `IF NOT EXISTS` / `TRUNCATE`-based setup; pair with Respawn for row-level reset |
| Calling `Types.InCurrentDomain()` in NetArchTest without forcing assembly load | Assembly may not be loaded; arch rule passes trivially (false green) | Use `Types.InAssembly(typeof(KnownType).Assembly)` to force load |
| Running Stryker without setting `"project"` in config — targeting the test project | Test helpers are mutated; unkillable mutants lower score and break threshold | Always set `"project"` to the source `.csproj`, never the test project |
| Registering WireMock stubs without resetting the server between tests | Later stubs shadow earlier ones; order-dependent, non-deterministic failures | Call `_server.Reset()` in constructor/setup or use a fresh server per class |
| Using `MockBehavior.Strict` across all mocks regardless of risk level | Every production API addition breaks all existing tests; high maintenance cost | Use Strict only for high-stakes contracts; use `VerifyNoOtherCalls()` for others |
| Writing NSubstitute `Arg.Is<T>` predicates without null-guards | Null arguments cause the predicate to throw; NSubstitute silently treats it as non-match and hides the root cause | Add `arg is null ? false : ...` null-guard at top of every `Arg.Is<T>` predicate lambda |

---

## Cycle 31 — 2026-05-14

### xUnit v3 — `[BeforeAfterTest]` Attribute for Per-Test Lifecycle Hooks

xUnit v3 re-introduced and formalized `BeforeAfterTestAttribute` as a composable, stackable attribute for injecting behavior before and after every decorated test method. Unlike constructor/`IAsyncLifetime`, `[BeforeAfterTest]` works at the method level, receives the `IXunitTest` context, and can be applied to entire classes (via a class-level attribute). This is the correct extension point for cross-cutting concerns such as ambient logging, database transaction scoping, or test-specific configuration overrides. [official]

```csharp
using System.Reflection;
using Xunit;
using Xunit.v3;

// 1. Define a reusable attribute
[AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Method | AttributeTargets.Class)]
public sealed class AmbientTenantAttribute : BeforeAfterTestAttribute
{
    private readonly string _tenantId;

    public AmbientTenantAttribute(string tenantId) => _tenantId = tenantId;

    public override ValueTask Before(MethodInfo methodUnderTest, IXunitTest test)
    {
        TenantContext.Current = _tenantId;   // set ambient tenant for the test
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }

    public override ValueTask After(MethodInfo methodUnderTest, IXunitTest test)
    {
        TenantContext.Current = null;        // always clean up, even on failure
        return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
    }
}

// 2. Apply at the method level — stacks with other BeforeAfterTestAttribute subclasses
public class OrderServiceTests
{
    [Fact]
    [AmbientTenant("tenant-acme")]
    public async Task GetOrders_ReturnsOnlyAcmeOrders()
    {
        var sut = new OrderService();
        var orders = await sut.GetOrdersForCurrentTenantAsync();

        Assert.All(orders, o => Assert.Equal("tenant-acme", o.TenantId));
    }

    [Fact]
    [AmbientTenant("tenant-globex")]
    public async Task GetOrders_ReturnsOnlyGlobexOrders()
    {
        var sut = new OrderService();
        var orders = await sut.GetOrdersForCurrentTenantAsync();

        Assert.All(orders, o => Assert.Equal("tenant-globex", o.TenantId));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `BeforeAfterTestAttribute` subclasses for cross-cutting concerns that apply to specific test methods or classes but do not require shared state (tenant context, locale, ambient feature flags). Do NOT use it to replace `IClassFixture<T>` for expensive shared resources (database connections, containers) — fixtures are the correct lifetime for those. Multiple `BeforeAfterTestAttribute` subclasses compose in declaration order (outermost declared = outermost wrap). Alternative: `IAsyncLifetime` for per-class setup/teardown, `IClassFixture<T>` for shared resources, custom xUnit `ITestFramework` for assembly-wide behavior. [official]

---

### NUnit 4 — `[CancelAfter]` Attribute for Per-Test Cancellation Deadlines

NUnit 4.1 introduced `[CancelAfter(int milliseconds)]` as the preferred replacement for `[Timeout]`. Unlike `[Timeout]`, which aborts the thread (unsafe, deprecated), `[CancelAfter]` injects a `CancellationToken` linked to the deadline into the test method's parameter. The test method can poll the token cooperatively — unsafe thread aborts are eliminated. [official]

```csharp
using NUnit.Framework;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;

[TestFixture]
public class DataImportServiceTests
{
    private DataImportService _sut = null!;

    [SetUp]
    public void SetUp() => _sut = new DataImportService();

    // [CancelAfter] injects a CancellationToken; the test fails if it does not
    // complete within 500 ms. No thread abort — cooperative cancellation only.
    [Test, CancelAfter(500)]
    public async Task ImportAsync_CancelsGracefully_WhenTokenSignalled(
        CancellationToken ct)
    {
        // ct is pre-linked to the 500 ms deadline
        var task = _sut.ImportAsync(largeDataSet: true, ct);

        // The [CancelAfter] deadline fires if the task does not finish in time
        await task;

        Assert.That(_sut.RecordsImported, Is.GreaterThan(0));
    }

    // Combine with [Retry] for flaky infrastructure tests with a time budget
    [Test, CancelAfter(2000), Retry(3)]
    public async Task PingExternalService_RespondsWithin2Seconds(
        CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var result = await _sut.PingAsync(ct);
        Assert.That(result.IsSuccess, Is.True);
    }

    // Assembly-level default: add [assembly: CancelAfter(10_000)] in AssemblyInfo.cs
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `[CancelAfter]` on any async test that calls I/O-bound code or external services — it prevents test hangs in CI without thread-unsafe aborts. Do NOT use it as a substitute for proper async design: if your production code does not honour `CancellationToken`, the test will still hang until the deadline fires rather than cancelling cooperatively. `[CancelAfter]` only helps when the code under test propagates the token. Alternative: `[Timeout]` (NUnit 3, thread-based, unsafe — avoid), TUnit `[Timeout]` (compile-time source-generated CT injection), xUnit `CancellationToken` via `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken`. [official]

---

### FluentAssertions — `Monitor()` for Event-Raised Assertions

FluentAssertions provides the `Monitor()` extension that subscribes to all public events on an object and records every invocation until disposed. Assertions can then verify that specific events were raised with specific arguments — without needing a manual event subscription in every test. [official]

```csharp
using FluentAssertions;
using Xunit;

public class InventoryTrackerTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void StockLevel_WhenDropsBelowThreshold_RaisesLowStockWarning()
    {
        var tracker = new InventoryTracker(threshold: 10);

        // Monitor() must be called BEFORE the act-step
        using var monitor = tracker.Monitor();

        tracker.UpdateStock(sku: "WIDGET-42", newLevel: 5);

        // Assert the event was raised at least once
        monitor.Should().Raise(nameof(tracker.LowStockWarning));
    }

    [Fact]
    public void StockLevel_WhenDropsBelowThreshold_RaisesEventWithCorrectArgs()
    {
        var tracker = new InventoryTracker(threshold: 10);
        using var monitor = tracker.Monitor();

        tracker.UpdateStock(sku: "WIDGET-42", newLevel: 3);

        // Assert event args carry the expected payload
        monitor.Should()
               .Raise(nameof(tracker.LowStockWarning))
               .WithSender(tracker)
               .WithArgs<LowStockEventArgs>(args => args.Sku == "WIDGET-42"
                                                 && args.CurrentLevel == 3);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void StockLevel_WhenAboveThreshold_DoesNotRaiseLowStockWarning()
    {
        var tracker = new InventoryTracker(threshold: 10);
        using var monitor = tracker.Monitor();

        tracker.UpdateStock(sku: "WIDGET-42", newLevel: 50);

        monitor.Should().NotRaise(nameof(tracker.LowStockWarning));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `Monitor()` any time production code communicates state changes via events (MVVM `INotifyPropertyChanged`, domain entities with .NET events, observable collections). Do NOT use it for components that communicate through `IObservable<T>` streams (Reactive Extensions) or `System.Threading.Channels` — those require different assertion approaches. `Monitor()` adds a reflection-based listener to every public event; dispose the monitor before asserting to stop recording. Alternative: manual event subscription with a captured flag/list, NSubstitute `Raise.EventWith` for raising events on substitutes. [official]

---

### Polly v8 — Chaos Engineering With `AddChaosFault` and `AddChaosLatency`

`Polly.Simmy` (chaos engineering extension for Polly v8) adds fault-injection and latency-injection strategies to a `ResiliencePipeline`. In tests you inject faults deterministically to verify that resilience policies and error-handling code behave correctly under adverse conditions — without needing a real failing dependency. [community]

```csharp
using Polly;
using Polly.Simmy;
using Polly.Simmy.Fault;
using Polly.Simmy.Latency;
using Xunit;

public class WeatherServiceResilienceTests
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task GetWeather_WhenDownstreamThrows_ReturnsCachedFallback()
    {
        // Pipeline: fallback (outermost) wraps chaos fault (innermost)
        var pipeline = new ResiliencePipelineBuilder<WeatherData>()
            .AddFallback(new FallbackStrategyOptions<WeatherData>
            {
                FallbackAction = _ => Outcome.FromResultAsValueTask(WeatherData.Stale),
                ShouldHandle   = new PredicateBuilder<WeatherData>()
                    .Handle<HttpRequestException>()
            })
            .AddChaosFault(new ChaosFaultStrategyOptions
            {
                InjectionRate    = 1.0,
                EnabledGenerator = _ => ValueTask.FromResult(true),
                FaultGenerator   = new FaultGenerator()
                    .AddException<HttpRequestException>()
            })
            .Build();

        var result = await pipeline.ExecuteAsync(
            async ct => await FetchWeatherAsync(ct),
            CancellationToken.None);

        Assert.Equal(WeatherData.Stale, result);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task GetWeather_WhenLatencyInjected_CircuitBreakerEventuallyTrips()
    {
        var breakerTripped = false;

        var pipeline = new ResiliencePipelineBuilder()
            .AddCircuitBreaker(new CircuitBreakerStrategyOptions
            {
                FailureRatio      = 0.5,
                MinimumThroughput = 2,
                SamplingDuration  = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10),
                BreakDuration     = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30),
                OnOpened = _ => { breakerTripped = true; return ValueTask.CompletedTask; }
            })
            .AddChaosLatency(new ChaosLatencyStrategyOptions
            {
                InjectionRate    = 1.0,
                EnabledGenerator = _ => ValueTask.FromResult(true),
                Latency          = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(35)
            })
            .Build();

        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
            try { await pipeline.ExecuteAsync(_ => ValueTask.CompletedTask); } catch { }

        Assert.True(breakerTripped, "Circuit breaker should have opened under injected latency");
    }

    private static ValueTask<WeatherData> FetchWeatherAsync(CancellationToken ct)
        => throw new NotImplementedException();
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use chaos strategies in dedicated resilience-spec test classes to verify that fallbacks, circuit breakers, and retry handlers engage correctly when dependencies misbehave. Do NOT inject chaos into the same pipeline used for ordinary unit tests — chaos strategies add execution overhead and make failures harder to attribute. `InjectionRate = 1.0` is for deterministic tests; fractional rates are for load and chaos experiments, not for CI unit tests. Polly v8 executes strategies outermost-first: if `AddChaosFault` is declared after the retry strategy in the builder chain, it is innermost and the retry policy wraps it — every fault is retried. If you want to bypass retries and go straight to the fallback, declare chaos outermost (first in the builder). Alternative: `FakeHttpMessageHandler` returning error `HttpResponseMessage` (lighter, no Polly.Simmy dependency), WireMock.Net returning 5xx responses. [community]

---

### ASP.NET Core — Output Cache Middleware Testing With `IOutputCacheStore`

ASP.NET Core's Output Cache middleware (introduced in .NET 7, enhanced through .NET 10) can be tested by asserting on cached HTTP response headers via `WebApplicationFactory` or by resolving `IOutputCacheStore` for direct tag-based eviction tests. The `WebApplicationFactory` approach verifies the end-to-end cache hit/miss cycle; the store approach verifies that specific cache tags are evicted. [official]

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OutputCaching;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using System.Net;
using Xunit;

public class ProductEndpointCacheTests : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    private readonly WebApplicationFactory<Program> _factory;

    public ProductEndpointCacheTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
    {
        _factory = factory.WithWebHostBuilder(builder =>
        {
            builder.ConfigureServices(services =>
            {
                services.AddOutputCache(options =>
                {
                    options.AddPolicy("ProductsPolicy",
                        p => p.Expire(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)).Tag("products"));
                });
            });
        });
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task GetProducts_SecondRequest_HasAgeHeaderIndicatingCacheHit()
    {
        var client = _factory.CreateClient();

        // Warm-up: first request populates the cache
        await client.GetAsync("/api/products");

        // Second request should be served from cache — Age header must be present
        var second = await client.GetAsync("/api/products");

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.OK, second.StatusCode);
        Assert.True(second.Headers.Contains("Age"),
            "Second response should have Age header (cache hit)");
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task EvictByTag_InvalidatesCachedProducts()
    {
        var client = _factory.CreateClient();

        // Populate the cache
        await client.GetAsync("/api/products");
        await client.GetAsync("/api/products");  // confirm cache hit

        // Resolve the store and evict by tag
        var store = _factory.Services.GetRequiredService<IOutputCacheStore>();
        await store.EvictByTagAsync("products", CancellationToken.None);

        // After eviction the next request is a cache miss — no Age header
        var afterEviction = await client.GetAsync("/api/products");
        Assert.False(afterEviction.Headers.Contains("Age"),
            "After tag eviction, response should be a cache miss (no Age header)");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Always send a warm-up request before asserting on `Age` headers — the first request to any `WebApplicationFactory` instance is always a cache miss. Test tag-based eviction explicitly when your application has event-driven cache invalidation (e.g., product updated → evict `"products"` tag). Do NOT use output cache testing as a substitute for unit-testing business logic — keep cache behavior in integration tests and domain logic in unit tests. Alternative: mock `IOutputCacheStore` with Moq to unit-test cache-key derivation logic in isolation. [official]

---

### ASP.NET Core — Rate Limiting Middleware Integration Testing

ASP.NET Core's `RateLimiter` middleware (added in .NET 7 via `System.Threading.RateLimiting`) enforces request throttling policies. Integration tests must exercise the middleware pipeline — not the limiter directly — to validate that `429 Too Many Requests` responses are returned with correct headers and that the endpoint is accessible below the configured limit. [official]

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting;
using System.Net;
using System.Threading.RateLimiting;
using Xunit;

public class RateLimitingIntegrationTests : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    private readonly HttpClient _client;

    public RateLimitingIntegrationTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
    {
        _client = factory.WithWebHostBuilder(builder =>
        {
            builder.ConfigureServices(services =>
            {
                services.AddRateLimiter(opts =>
                {
                    opts.AddFixedWindowLimiter("fixed", cfg =>
                    {
                        cfg.PermitLimit          = 2;
                        cfg.Window               = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10);
                        cfg.QueueProcessingOrder = QueueProcessingOrder.OldestFirst;
                        cfg.QueueLimit           = 0;
                    });
                    opts.RejectionStatusCode = StatusCodes.Status429TooManyRequests;
                });
            });
        }).CreateClient();
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Endpoint_BelowRateLimit_Returns200()
    {
        var r1 = await _client.GetAsync("/api/data");
        var r2 = await _client.GetAsync("/api/data");

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.OK, r1.StatusCode);
        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.OK, r2.StatusCode);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Endpoint_ExceedsRateLimit_Returns429WithRetryAfterHeader()
    {
        // Exhaust the 2-permit window
        await _client.GetAsync("/api/data");
        await _client.GetAsync("/api/data");

        // Third request exceeds the limit
        var throttled = await _client.GetAsync("/api/data");

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.TooManyRequests, throttled.StatusCode);
        Assert.True(throttled.Headers.Contains("Retry-After"),
            "429 response must include Retry-After header per RFC 6585");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Test rate limiting at the integration level — the `WebApplicationFactory` spins up the real middleware pipeline so the limiter actually executes. Do NOT assert on exact `Retry-After` values in CI environments where clock skew makes the value non-deterministic; assert only on header presence or a `>= 0` numeric range. When testing per-user or per-IP policies, simulate different callers by setting a custom `RemoteIpAddress` via a thin custom middleware added in `WithWebHostBuilder`. Alternative: unit-test `FixedWindowRateLimiter` directly for token-acquisition logic; reserve integration tests for middleware plumbing. [official]

---

### ASP.NET Core — Keyed DI Services With `WebApplicationFactory`

.NET 8 introduced keyed dependency injection via `AddKeyedSingleton<T>`, `AddKeyedScoped<T>`, and `AddKeyedTransient<T>`. Integration tests that need to resolve a specific keyed implementation or swap one key's registration must use `GetRequiredKeyedService<T>` on the service provider or override keyed registrations inside `WithWebHostBuilder`. [official]

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Xunit;

// Production registrations in Program.cs (assumed):
//   builder.Services.AddKeyedSingleton<IPaymentGateway, StripeGateway>("stripe");
//   builder.Services.AddKeyedSingleton<IPaymentGateway, PayPalGateway>("paypal");

public class KeyedDiIntegrationTests : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    private readonly WebApplicationFactory<Program> _factory;

    public KeyedDiIntegrationTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
    {
        _factory = factory.WithWebHostBuilder(builder =>
        {
            builder.ConfigureServices(services =>
            {
                // Override only the "stripe" key with a test double
                services.AddKeyedSingleton<IPaymentGateway, StubPaymentGateway>("stripe");
            });
        });
    }

    [Fact]
    public void StripeGateway_CanBeResolvedByKey_AsTestDouble()
    {
        var gateway = _factory.Services
            .GetRequiredKeyedService<IPaymentGateway>("stripe");

        Assert.IsType<StubPaymentGateway>(gateway);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void PayPalGateway_IsNotAffectedByStripeOverride()
    {
        // PayPal registration from production code still resolves unchanged
        var paypal = _factory.Services
            .GetRequiredKeyedService<IPaymentGateway>("paypal");

        Assert.IsType<PayPalGateway>(paypal);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task CheckoutEndpoint_RoutesStripePaymentToStub()
    {
        var client = _factory.CreateClient();

        var response = await client.PostAsJsonAsync("/api/checkout",
            new { Amount = 100, Gateway = "stripe" });

        response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
    }

    private sealed class StubPaymentGateway : IPaymentGateway
    {
        public Task<PaymentResult> ChargeAsync(decimal amount, CancellationToken ct)
            => Task.FromResult(new PaymentResult { Success = true, TransactionId = "stub-txn" });
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use keyed DI overrides when your application selects an implementation at runtime based on a string key (payment gateways, notification channels, storage providers). Do NOT attempt to replace a keyed registration via the un-keyed `AddSingleton<IPaymentGateway>` path — un-keyed and keyed registrations are separate collections; the un-keyed override will not intercept keyed resolution. Always override using the matching `AddKeyedSingleton/Scoped/Transient` call with the same key string. Alternative: feature flags to swap implementations, `IServiceProviderIsKeyedService` for conditional resolution in production code. [official]

---

### Moq — `SetupSequence` for Ordered Multi-Call Return Values

`SetupSequence` configures a mock to return different values (or throw different exceptions) on successive invocations of the same member. This is essential when testing retry logic, paginated enumeration, or any code that calls the same method multiple times and expects different responses each time. [community]

```csharp
using Moq;
using Xunit;

public interface ITokenRefresher
{
    Task<string> GetAccessTokenAsync(CancellationToken ct);
}

public class ApiClientRetryTests
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task SendRequest_WhenTokenExpiredOnFirstCall_RefreshesAndRetries()
    {
        var refresher = new Mock<ITokenRefresher>();

        // First call: expired token. Second call: fresh token.
        refresher
            .SetupSequence(r => r.GetAccessTokenAsync(It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()))
            .ReturnsAsync("expired-token-abc")
            .ReturnsAsync("fresh-token-xyz");

        var sut = new ApiClient(refresher.Object);
        var result = await sut.GetDataAsync(CancellationToken.None);

        refresher.Verify(
            r => r.GetAccessTokenAsync(It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()),
            Times.Exactly(2));
        Assert.Equal("success", result.Status);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task PaginatedQuery_DrainsPagesUntilEmpty()
    {
        var repo = new Mock<IProductRepository>();

        // Three calls: two pages then empty sentinel
        repo.SetupSequence(r => r.GetPageAsync(It.IsAny<int>(), It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()))
            .ReturnsAsync(new[] { new Product("A"), new Product("B") })
            .ReturnsAsync(new[] { new Product("C") })
            .ReturnsAsync(Array.Empty<Product>());

        var sut = new ProductAggregator(repo.Object);
        var all = await sut.GetAllAsync(CancellationToken.None);

        Assert.Equal(3, all.Count);
        repo.Verify(r => r.GetPageAsync(It.IsAny<int>(), It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()),
            Times.Exactly(3));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `SetupSequence` when the code under test calls the same method multiple times and each call should produce a distinct outcome — retry handlers, pagination loops, polling loops. Do NOT use `SetupSequence` as a workaround for methods that should have different parameters on successive calls; use separate `Setup` calls with `It.Is<T>` parameter matching instead, which produces clearer failure messages. Once the sequence is exhausted, Moq returns the default value with `MockBehavior.Loose` or throws `MockException` with `MockBehavior.Strict`. Alternative: NSubstitute's `Returns(v1, v2, v3)` multi-value shorthand (same semantic, terser syntax), a `Callback` with an index counter (more flexible for complex interleaving). [community]

---

### ASP.NET Core — `ProblemDetails` Response Shape Assertion Pattern

ASP.NET Core maps exceptions and validation failures to `ProblemDetails` (RFC 7807) responses with `Content-Type: application/problem+json`. Integration tests should assert on the full `ProblemDetails` payload — not just the status code — to catch regressions in `type`, `title`, `detail`, and custom extension members. [official]

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Json;
using Xunit;

public class ProblemDetailsAssertionTests : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    private readonly HttpClient _client;

    public ProblemDetailsAssertionTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
        => _client = factory.CreateClient();

    [Fact]
    public async Task CreateOrder_WithInvalidPayload_Returns422WithValidationProblem()
    {
        var response = await _client.PostAsJsonAsync("/api/orders",
            new { Quantity = -1, ProductId = "" });

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.UnprocessableContent, response.StatusCode);
        Assert.Equal("application/problem+json",
            response.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType);

        // Deserialize as ValidationProblemDetails to access the Errors dictionary
        var problem = await response.Content
            .ReadFromJsonAsync<ValidationProblemDetails>();

        Assert.NotNull(problem);
        Assert.Contains("Quantity", problem!.Errors.Keys);
        Assert.Contains("ProductId", problem.Errors.Keys);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task GetOrder_WhenNotFound_Returns404WithNonEmptyTitle()
    {
        var response = await _client.GetAsync("/api/orders/99999");

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.NotFound, response.StatusCode);

        var problem = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<ProblemDetails>();

        Assert.NotNull(problem);
        Assert.Equal(404, problem!.Status);
        Assert.False(string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(problem.Title),
            "ProblemDetails.Title must not be empty for 404 responses");
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task CreateOrder_WhenDomainRuleViolated_Returns409WithCustomExtension()
    {
        var response = await _client.PostAsJsonAsync("/api/orders",
            new { Quantity = 1, ProductId = "OUT-OF-STOCK-SKU" });

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Conflict, response.StatusCode);

        // Use JsonElement to assert on custom ProblemDetails extension members
        var json = await response.Content
            .ReadFromJsonAsync<System.Text.Json.JsonElement>();
        Assert.True(json.TryGetProperty("errorCode", out var code),
            "Conflict response must include custom 'errorCode' extension member");
        Assert.Equal("OUT_OF_STOCK", code.GetString());
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Always assert on `Content-Type: application/problem+json` in addition to the status code — the media type is the contract clients use to distinguish RFC 7807 errors from generic JSON bodies. Deserialize as `ValidationProblemDetails` (not just `ProblemDetails`) when the endpoint uses `Results.ValidationProblem()` or model-state validation, because `ValidationProblemDetails.Errors` is absent from the base `ProblemDetails` type. Do NOT assert on `ProblemDetails.Detail` when the value is environment-dependent (stack traces, inner exception messages). Alternative: FluentAssertions `BeEquivalentTo` on a manually constructed `ProblemDetails` object for inline expected-value comparisons. [official]

---

### ASP.NET Core — Custom Middleware Testing in Isolation via `TestServer`

Middleware components can be tested in isolation without the full application pipeline by constructing a minimal `IWebHostBuilder` that only includes the middleware under test and a terminal stub handler. This is faster and more precise than running the full `WebApplicationFactory`. [official]

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost;
using System.Net;
using Xunit;

// Middleware under test: adds a correlation ID header if absent
public class CorrelationIdMiddleware
{
    private readonly RequestDelegate _next;
    public CorrelationIdMiddleware(RequestDelegate next) => _next = next;

    public async Task InvokeAsync(HttpContext ctx)
    {
        if (!ctx.Request.Headers.ContainsKey("X-Correlation-Id"))
            ctx.Request.Headers["X-Correlation-Id"] = Guid.NewGuid().ToString();

        ctx.Response.Headers["X-Correlation-Id"] =
            ctx.Request.Headers["X-Correlation-Id"].ToString();

        await _next(ctx);
    }
}

public class CorrelationIdMiddlewareTests
{
    private static TestServer BuildTestServer() =>
        new TestServer(new WebHostBuilder()
            .Configure(app =>
            {
                app.UseMiddleware<CorrelationIdMiddleware>();
                app.Run(ctx =>
                {
                    ctx.Response.StatusCode = 200;
                    return Task.CompletedTask;
                });
            }));

    [Fact]
    public async Task Request_WithoutCorrelationHeader_AddsGuidToResponse()
    {
        using var server = BuildTestServer();
        var client = server.CreateClient();

        var response = await client.GetAsync("/");

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.OK, response.StatusCode);
        Assert.True(response.Headers.Contains("X-Correlation-Id"),
            "Middleware must add X-Correlation-Id to response when absent on request");

        var value = response.Headers.GetValues("X-Correlation-Id").Single();
        Assert.True(Guid.TryParse(value, out _), "Correlation ID must be a valid GUID");
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Request_WithExistingCorrelationHeader_PropagatesIt()
    {
        using var server = BuildTestServer();
        var client = server.CreateClient();

        var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, "/");
        request.Headers.Add("X-Correlation-Id", "trace-abc-123");

        var response = await client.SendAsync(request);

        var returned = response.Headers.GetValues("X-Correlation-Id").Single();
        Assert.Equal("trace-abc-123", returned);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `TestServer`-based middleware isolation tests when the middleware is complex enough to warrant its own test class but does not depend on application services. Do NOT test middleware via the full `WebApplicationFactory` pipeline when the goal is to verify a single middleware behaviour in isolation — full pipeline tests are slower and make failures harder to attribute. If the middleware requires DI-resolved services, configure them via `ConfigureServices` on the `WebHostBuilder`. Alternative: `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` for end-to-end middleware ordering tests, `DefaultHttpContext` for pure-unit middleware tests with no HTTP infrastructure. [official]

---

### `DelegatingHandler` Test Double — Inspecting and Stubbing the `HttpClient` Pipeline

`DelegatingHandler` allows inserting custom logic into the `HttpClient` message pipeline. A test-double delegating handler can capture outgoing requests, assert on their shape, and return a controlled `HttpResponseMessage` without any network I/O. This is lighter than WireMock.Net and works without a TCP listener. [community]

```csharp
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http;
using Xunit;

// Reusable recording handler: captures all requests, returns a stub response
public sealed class RecordingHandler : DelegatingHandler
{
    private readonly HttpStatusCode _statusCode;
    private readonly string         _responseBody;
    public readonly List<(HttpMethod Method, Uri? Uri, string? Body)> Captured = [];

    public RecordingHandler(
        HttpStatusCode statusCode   = HttpStatusCode.OK,
        string         responseBody = "{}")
        : base(new NoOpInnerHandler())
    {
        _statusCode   = statusCode;
        _responseBody = responseBody;
    }

    protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
        HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        // Read body BEFORE returning — content is disposed after SendAsync returns
        var body = request.Content is not null
            ? await request.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(ct)
            : null;

        Captured.Add((request.Method, request.RequestUri, body));

        return new HttpResponseMessage(_statusCode)
        {
            Content = new StringContent(_responseBody,
                System.Text.Encoding.UTF8, "application/json")
        };
    }

    private sealed class NoOpInnerHandler : HttpMessageHandler
    {
        protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
            HttpRequestMessage r, CancellationToken ct)
            => throw new InvalidOperationException("Requests must not reach the inner handler");
    }
}

public class GithubApiClientTests
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task GetUser_SendsCorrectAuthorizationHeader()
    {
        var handler = new RecordingHandler(
            HttpStatusCode.OK, """{"login":"octocat","id":1}""");
        var httpClient = new HttpClient(handler)
        {
            BaseAddress = new Uri("https://api.github.com")
        };

        var client = new GithubApiClient(httpClient, apiToken: "ghp_test_token");
        await client.GetUserAsync("octocat", CancellationToken.None);

        Assert.Single(handler.Captured);
        var (method, uri, _) = handler.Captured[0];
        Assert.Equal(HttpMethod.Get, method);
        Assert.Equal("/users/octocat", uri?.PathAndQuery);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `DelegatingHandler` test doubles when you want to assert on outgoing `HttpRequestMessage` shape (headers, URI, body, method) or return controlled responses without a network or TCP listener. Always read `request.Content` to a string inside `SendAsync` before returning — the content is disposed after the call completes, and reading it in the assertion phase throws `ObjectDisposedException`. Do NOT use this approach when you need to test the `IHttpClientFactory` named/typed client resolution pipeline end-to-end; use `ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler` via `WebApplicationFactory` for that. Alternative: `RichardSzalay.MockHttp` (higher-level API, pattern-based matching), WireMock.Net (wire-level HTTP inspection with a real TCP listener). [community]

---

### `IAsyncEnumerable` Streaming Endpoint Testing

ASP.NET Core supports returning `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` from minimal API handlers — the runtime streams each item as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Integration tests must consume the response body as a stream rather than as a single JSON document; `HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead` ensures the body is not buffered. [official]

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;
using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http;
using System.Text.Json;
using Xunit;

public class StreamingEndpointTests : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    private readonly HttpClient _client;

    public StreamingEndpointTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
        => _client = factory.CreateClient();

    [Fact]
    public async Task StreamProducts_ReturnsNdjsonItems()
    {
        // ResponseHeadersRead: do not buffer the body — receive it as a stream
        var response = await _client.GetAsync("/api/products/stream",
            HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead);

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.OK, response.StatusCode);
        Assert.Equal("application/x-ndjson",
            response.Content.Headers.ContentType?.MediaType);

        await using var stream = await response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync();
        using var reader = new System.IO.StreamReader(stream);

        var products = new List<Product>();
        string? line;
        while ((line = await reader.ReadLineAsync()) is not null)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(line)) continue;
            var item = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Product>(line,
                new JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true });
            if (item is not null)
                products.Add(item);
        }

        Assert.NotEmpty(products);
        Assert.All(products, p => Assert.False(string.IsNullOrEmpty(p.Sku)));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task StreamProducts_FirstItemArrivesBeforeStreamCompletes()
    {
        // Verify the server sends the first item without waiting for the full stream
        var response = await _client.GetAsync("/api/products/stream",
            HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead);

        await using var stream = await response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync();
        using var reader = new System.IO.StreamReader(stream);

        // Read only the first line — endpoint must not buffer all items before sending any
        var firstLine = await reader.ReadLineAsync();

        Assert.False(string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(firstLine),
            "Server must stream the first item without buffering the full response");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Always use `HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead` when testing streaming endpoints — without it, `HttpClient` buffers the entire response in memory and the test times out on long streams. Use NDJSON (`application/x-ndjson`) as the content type for `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` endpoints; JSON arrays require the full payload before deserialization can begin. Do NOT assert on exact item counts for unbounded streams in unit tests; assert that at least one item was received and that each item satisfies the schema contract. Alternative: SSE (`TypedResults.ServerSentEvents`) for browser-compatible push (already covered in Cycle 29), JSON array responses for small collections that can be buffered without issue. [official]

---

### xUnit v3 — `Assert.Fail` and `Assert.Skip` for Conditional Test Outcomes

xUnit v3 added `Assert.Fail(string reason)` and `Assert.Skip(string reason)` as first-class assertion methods, removing the need for `throw new XunitException(...)` for forced failures and for attribute-based skips when the skip condition is only known at runtime. Both methods integrate with xUnit's result reporting infrastructure. [official]

```csharp
using Xunit;

public class ConditionalTestOutcomeTests
{
    // Assert.Skip for runtime-conditional skip — environment check, license, feature flag
    [Fact]
    public async Task ImportFromS3_OnlyRunsWhenAwsCredentialsPresent()
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID")))
            Assert.Skip("AWS credentials not configured — skipping S3 integration test");

        var importer = new S3DataImporter();
        var count = await importer.ImportAsync("my-bucket", CancellationToken.None);

        Assert.True(count > 0, "Import must return at least one record");
    }

    // Assert.Fail as explicit "should not reach here" guard in exception tests
    [Fact]
    public async Task ProcessOrder_WhenUnknownStatus_DoesNotThrow()
    {
        var processor = new OrderProcessor();

        try
        {
            await processor.ProcessAsync(new Order { Status = OrderStatus.Unknown });
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            Assert.Fail($"ProcessAsync must not throw for unknown status. Threw: {ex}");
        }
    }

    // Assert.Skip inside a theory for data-driven conditional skips
    [Theory]
    [InlineData("feature-x", true)]
    [InlineData("feature-y", false)]
    public void Feature_WhenEnabled_IsRecognizedByRegistry(string feature, bool enabled)
    {
        if (!enabled)
            Assert.Skip($"Feature '{feature}' is disabled in this environment");

        var registry = new FeatureRegistry();
        Assert.True(registry.IsEnabled(feature));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `Assert.Skip` for runtime-conditional test skipping where the skip condition cannot be known at compile time (environment variables, OS checks, license checks, feature flags). Use `Assert.Fail` as an explicit unreachable-code guard in try/catch blocks where `throw` would change the method's return-type flow. Do NOT use `Assert.Skip` as a lazy "not implemented yet" marker — xUnit's `[Skip("TODO: ...")]` attribute is more visible in test reports and clearly marks intent. Alternative: `[SkippableFact]` from the `Xunit.SkippableFact` NuGet for xUnit v2, NUnit `Assume.That()` for conditional skip semantics. [official]

---

### MSTest v3 — `[ClassInitialize(InheritanceBehavior.BeforeEachDerivedClass)]` for Base-Class Setup Sharing

MSTest v3 allows `[ClassInitialize]` in a base class with `InheritanceBehavior.BeforeEachDerivedClass`. This runs the base initializer once per derived test class before that class's own `[ClassInitialize]`, enabling shared expensive setup (containers, HTTP clients, database connections) without inheritance ceremony. [official]

```csharp
using Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting;

// Base class: database connection initialized once per derived class
[TestClass]
public abstract class DatabaseIntegrationBase
{
    protected static string ConnectionString { get; private set; } = "";

    // Runs before [ClassInitialize] in every derived class
    [ClassInitialize(InheritanceBehavior.BeforeEachDerivedClass)]
    public static async Task BaseClassInitialize(TestContext context)
    {
        ConnectionString = await TestDatabase.GetConnectionStringAsync();
        context.WriteLine($"Database ready: {ConnectionString[..Math.Min(40, ConnectionString.Length)]}...");
    }

    [ClassCleanup(InheritanceBehavior.BeforeEachDerivedClass)]
    public static async Task BaseClassCleanup()
    {
        await TestDatabase.CleanupAsync();
    }
}

// Derived class: ConnectionString is already set when its own [ClassInitialize] runs
[TestClass]
public class OrderRepositoryTests : DatabaseIntegrationBase
{
    private static OrderRepository _repo = null!;

    [ClassInitialize]
    public static void Initialize(TestContext ctx)
    {
        // Base initializer has already run — ConnectionString is available
        _repo = new OrderRepository(ConnectionString);
    }

    [TestMethod]
    public async Task Insert_ThenFindById_ReturnsMatchingOrder()
    {
        var order = new Order { CustomerId = 42, Total = 99.99m };
        var id    = await _repo.InsertAsync(order);
        var found = await _repo.FindByIdAsync(id);

        Assert.IsNotNull(found);
        Assert.AreEqual(order.Total, found.Total);
    }

    [TestMethod]
    public async Task Delete_ExistingOrder_RemovesFromDatabase()
    {
        var id = await _repo.InsertAsync(new Order { CustomerId = 1, Total = 10m });
        await _repo.DeleteAsync(id);

        var found = await _repo.FindByIdAsync(id);
        Assert.IsNull(found, "Deleted order must not be retrievable");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff / when to use:** Use `InheritanceBehavior.BeforeEachDerivedClass` when multiple test classes share the same expensive setup and you want to avoid duplicating initializers. Do NOT use this pattern when the base-class setup is cheap (simple object creation) — the inheritance complexity adds confusion without benefit. MSTest runs `[ClassInitialize]` on all test classes including those with zero test methods; decorate base classes with `[TestClass]` only if they contain their own `[TestMethod]` declarations. Alternative: `IClassFixture<T>` + xUnit `[Collection]` for shared fixtures without inheritance, NUnit `[OneTimeSetUp]` in a base class (NUnit supports base-class setup natively without a flag). [official]

---

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 31

**FluentAssertions `Monitor()` does not capture events raised before `Monitor()` is called — arrange order matters [community]** — `using var monitor = obj.Monitor()` begins recording from the moment of the call. Any event raised during object construction, or before the `using` statement, is not captured in the recording. WHY it causes problems: tests that call `Monitor()` after triggering a state change that fires an event always fail with "event was never raised", even when the event genuinely fired. Fix: always call `Monitor()` before the act-step (the state-mutating call that is expected to raise the event), never after.

**NUnit `[CancelAfter]` only injects a `CancellationToken` when the test method signature declares it — omitting the parameter silently disables cooperative cancellation [community]** — If a test method decorated with `[CancelAfter(500)]` does not declare a `CancellationToken ct` parameter, NUnit still enforces the timeout via an internal cancellation source, but the code under test never receives the token. WHY it causes problems: async code that calls `Task.Delay` or network I/O with `CancellationToken.None` will not be interrupted when the deadline fires; the test only fails after the full underlying I/O timeout, not at the `[CancelAfter]` boundary. Fix: always declare `CancellationToken ct` in every async test method annotated with `[CancelAfter]` and propagate it to all async calls.

**Polly v8 `AddChaosFault` position in the builder chain changes whether retries are bypassed or consumed — undocumented ordering gotcha [community]** — Polly v8 executes strategies outermost-first (first declared = outermost). If `AddChaosFault` is declared after `AddRetry` in the builder chain (making it innermost), every injected fault is retried by the retry strategy — consuming all retry attempts before the fallback fires. If chaos is declared before retry (outermost), it bypasses retries entirely. WHY it causes problems: chaos tests designed to verify that the fallback fires after all retries are exhausted produce non-deterministic results depending on the chaos strategy's position in the builder. Fix: always draw the strategy execution order (first declared = outermost wrapping) before writing chaos tests; comment the intended order explicitly.
