## Cycle 52 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 181 — xUnit v3 `TheoryData<T1, T2>` Strongly-Typed Theory Input for Compile-Time Safe Parameterised Tests [official]

xUnit v3 introduces `TheoryData<T>` and its generic overloads (`TheoryData<T1, T2>`, etc.) as a type-safe replacement for `object[]` rows in `[MemberData]` sources. When a `[Theory]` method parameter count or type changes, the `TheoryData` property fails to compile immediately rather than surfacing a runtime `InvalidOperationException` on test discovery. This removes an entire class of silent test-data breakage that previously only appeared when the test suite ran.

```csharp
public class OrderPricingTheoryData : TheoryData<string, decimal, decimal>
{
    public OrderPricingTheoryData()
    {
        Add("standard",  100m, 100m);   // no markup
        Add("express",   100m, 115m);   // +15% surcharge
        Add("overnight", 100m, 135m);   // +35% surcharge
        Add("same-day",  100m, 150m);   // +50% surcharge
    }
}

public class ShippingCostCalculatorTests
{
    [Theory]
    [ClassData(typeof(OrderPricingTheoryData))]
    public void Calculate_KnownTier_ProducesCorrectTotal(
        string tier, decimal basePrice, decimal expectedTotal)
    {
        var calc = new ShippingCostCalculator();
        var result = calc.Calculate(tier, basePrice);
        Assert.Equal(expectedTotal, result.Total);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `TheoryData<T>` locks parameter types at declaration time — if a theory method needs to accept `object` for mixed-type rows (e.g., comparing `int` and `long` overloads), you must fall back to `object[]` or define multiple theory methods. The compile-time safety gain is worth the constraint in the majority of data-driven tests where all rows share the same shape. [official]

---

### Pattern 182 — NUnit 4 `[CancelAfter]` Attribute for Per-Test Timeout With `CancellationToken` Injection [official]

NUnit 4.1 introduced `[CancelAfter(ms)]` as a first-class replacement for the older `[Timeout]` attribute. Unlike `[Timeout]`, which aborts the test thread, `[CancelAfter]` injects a pre-cancelled `CancellationToken` into any test parameter named `cancellationToken`, enabling cooperative cancellation of async operations without thread abort exceptions. This makes timeout behaviour observable and assertable within the test body rather than opaque to the runner.

```csharp
[TestFixture]
public class PaymentGatewayClientTests
{
    private readonly FakePaymentGatewayServer _server = new();

    [CancelAfter(2_000)]
    [TestCase("visa")]
    [TestCase("mastercard")]
    public async Task Charge_SlowGateway_CancelsWithinTimeout(
        string cardBrand, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        _server.SimulateDelay(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
        var client = new PaymentGatewayClient(_server.BaseAddress);

        await Assert.ThatAsync(
            () => client.ChargeAsync(cardBrand, 99.99m, cancellationToken),
            Throws.InstanceOf<OperationCanceledException>());
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `[CancelAfter]` requires the SUT and all awaited code to respect `CancellationToken` propagation — a SUT that ignores cancellation tokens will run to completion regardless of the attribute, silently exceeding the intended timeout without triggering the cancellation assertion. Audit the call chain for `CancellationToken.None` hardcodes before relying on `[CancelAfter]` as a safety net. [official]

---

### Pattern 183 — Moq `Capture.In<T>` for Recording Arguments Passed to Mocked Methods [official]

Moq's `Capture.In<T>(list)` callback parameter captures every argument passed to a mocked method into a `List<T>` without requiring a separate `Setup` callback. This is preferable to embedding assertion logic inside a `Callback` lambda because it cleanly separates the capture (arrange) from the assertion (assert), and the captured list can be inspected with FluentAssertions or xUnit assertions after the act phase.

```csharp
[Fact]
public void ProcessBatch_PublishesOneEventPerOrder()
{
    var publishedEvents = new List<OrderProcessedEvent>();
    var mockBus = new Mock<IEventBus>();
    mockBus
        .Setup(b => b.Publish(Capture.In(publishedEvents)));

    var processor = new OrderBatchProcessor(mockBus.Object);
    var orders = Enumerable.Range(1, 3)
        .Select(i => new Order { Id = $"ORD-{i}", Amount = i * 10m })
        .ToList();

    processor.ProcessBatch(orders);

    Assert.Equal(3, publishedEvents.Count);
    Assert.All(publishedEvents, e => Assert.NotNull(e.OrderId));
    Assert.Equal(new[] { "ORD-1", "ORD-2", "ORD-3" },
        publishedEvents.Select(e => e.OrderId));
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `Capture.In` only captures the argument at the moment of the call — if the SUT mutates the object after publishing (e.g., setting `Order.ProcessedAt`), the captured value reflects the post-mutation state because it holds a reference. Use `Capture.In` with value types or immutable records, or clone objects in a `Callback` when mutation after publication is possible. [official]

---

### Pattern 184 — FluentAssertions `BeEquivalentTo` With `Using<T>(comparer)` for Custom Per-Type Equality [official]

FluentAssertions `BeEquivalentTo` supports per-type custom equality via `.Using<T>(IEqualityComparer<T>)` in the equivalency options lambda. This lets you apply domain-specific equality (e.g., case-insensitive email comparison, currency rounding) to nested value types without implementing `IEquatable<T>` on the domain model itself. The comparer is applied recursively wherever that type appears in the object graph.

```csharp
[Fact]
public void PlaceOrder_CreatesCustomerRecordWithNormalisedEmail()
{
    var service = new OrderService(new InMemoryCustomerRepository());
    var command = new PlaceOrderCommand(
        Email: "USER@EXAMPLE.COM",
        Items: new[] { new OrderItem("SKU-1", 2) });

    var result = service.PlaceOrder(command);

    result.Customer.Should().BeEquivalentTo(
        new Customer { Email = "user@example.com", IsVerified = false },
        opts => opts
            .Using<string>(ctx =>
                ctx.Subject.Should().BeEquivalentTo(ctx.Expectation,
                    StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
            .WhenTypeIs<string>()
            .Excluding(c => c.Id)
            .Excluding(c => c.CreatedAt));
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Applying a custom comparer via `WhenTypeIs<string>()` affects every `string` property in the graph — including properties you did not intend to compare case-insensitively (e.g., `Status`, `ErrorCode`). Scope comparer application with `.When(info => info.Path.EndsWith("Email"))` to constrain it to the intended property path. [official]

---

### Pattern 185 — Testcontainers.NET `WithNetwork` and `WithNetworkAliases` for Multi-Container Integration Tests [official]

Testcontainers.NET supports creating an isolated Docker network shared by multiple containers via `new NetworkBuilder().Build()`. Assigning network aliases with `WithNetworkAliases("alias")` allows containers to address each other by hostname rather than by dynamically assigned IP, making multi-service integration tests (e.g., API + database + cache) reproducible across machines with no hardcoded ports.

```csharp
public class OrderApiIntegrationTests : IAsyncLifetime
{
    private readonly INetwork _network = new NetworkBuilder().Build();
    private PostgreSqlContainer _db = null!;
    private RedisContainer _cache = null!;

    public async Task InitializeAsync()
    {
        await _network.CreateAsync();

        _db = new PostgreSqlBuilder()
            .WithNetwork(_network)
            .WithNetworkAliases("postgres")
            .Build();

        _cache = new RedisBuilder()
            .WithNetwork(_network)
            .WithNetworkAliases("redis")
            .Build();

        await Task.WhenAll(_db.StartAsync(), _cache.StartAsync());
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task GetOrder_CachePopulated_ReturnsCachedResult()
    {
        var factory = new WebApplicationFactory<Program>()
            .WithWebHostBuilder(b => b.UseSetting(
                "ConnectionStrings:Db", _db.GetConnectionString()));
        var client = factory.CreateClient();
        var response = await client.GetAsync("/orders/ORD-001");
        response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
    }

    public async Task DisposeAsync()
    {
        await _db.DisposeAsync();
        await _cache.DisposeAsync();
        await _network.DisposeAsync();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Shared Docker networks add container startup latency — creating and tearing down the network on every test class adds ~200–500 ms depending on the Docker daemon. Use `IClassFixture<T>` to share the network across tests in the same class, and `ICollectionFixture<T>` for sharing across multiple test classes in the same assembly. [official]

---

### Pattern 186 — MSTest v3 `[DynamicData]` With `DynamicDataSourceType.Method` for Computed Parameterised Tests [official]

MSTest v3 `[DynamicData]` with `DynamicDataSourceType.Method` allows a static method returning `IEnumerable<object[]>` to generate test parameters programmatically. Unlike `[DataRow]`, which requires compile-time literal values, `[DynamicData]` supports runtime-computed inputs such as reading from embedded JSON resources, generating edge cases algorithmically, or building parameter combinations from domain constants.

```csharp
[TestClass]
public class TaxCalculatorTests
{
    private static IEnumerable<object[]> GetTaxBracketCases()
    {
        // Computed from the current tax year's thresholds
        var brackets = TaxBracket.CurrentYear();
        foreach (var bracket in brackets)
        {
            yield return new object[]
            {
                bracket.MinIncome + 1,    // just above lower bound
                bracket.ExpectedRate,
                $"income just above £{bracket.MinIncome:N0} bracket"
            };
            yield return new object[]
            {
                bracket.MaxIncome - 1,    // just below upper bound
                bracket.ExpectedRate,
                $"income just below £{bracket.MaxIncome:N0} bracket"
            };
        }
    }

    [TestMethod]
    [DynamicData(nameof(GetTaxBracketCases), DynamicDataSourceType.Method)]
    public void Calculate_BoundaryIncome_ReturnsCorrectRate(
        decimal income, decimal expectedRate, string scenario)
    {
        var calc = new TaxCalculator();
        Assert.AreEqual(expectedRate, calc.CalculateRate(income),
            $"Failed for scenario: {scenario}");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `[DynamicData]` method bodies run at test discovery time, not test execution time — if the method throws, all test cases in the method are reported as discovery failures rather than test failures, which can obscure the root cause. Wrap the data source method body in a try/catch that rethrows as `InvalidOperationException` with a descriptive message to surface discovery failures clearly in Test Explorer. [official]

---

### Pattern 187 — NSubstitute `ReceivedWithAnyArgs` for Call-Count Verification When Argument Values Are Irrelevant [official]

NSubstitute `ReceivedWithAnyArgs(n)` verifies that a substitute received exactly `n` calls regardless of argument values, without requiring `Arg.Any<T>()` placeholders for each parameter. This is the correct pattern for auditing that a side-effectful method (e.g., `logger.Log`, `auditService.Record`) was called the expected number of times when argument content is covered by separate, targeted assertions.

```csharp
[Fact]
public void DeleteAccount_SendsTwoAuditEvents_AndOneEmail()
{
    var audit = Substitute.For<IAuditService>();
    var email = Substitute.For<IEmailService>();
    var service = new AccountDeletionService(audit, email);

    service.Delete(accountId: "ACC-999");

    // Verify call counts without constraining argument values here;
    // argument content is validated in separate focused tests
    audit.ReceivedWithAnyArgs(2).Record(default!, default!);
    email.ReceivedWithAnyArgs(1).Send(default!, default!, default!);
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `ReceivedWithAnyArgs` provides no safety if the implementation calls the method with incorrect arguments — it only verifies quantity. Always pair call-count assertions with at least one argument-capturing or argument-matching assertion on the most important call to prevent argument regressions from going undetected. [official]

---

### Pattern 188 — FluentAssertions `ExecutionTime` Assertion for In-Process Performance Budgets [official]

FluentAssertions provides `.ExecutionTimeOf(action)` and `.ExecutionTime()` to assert that a synchronous or asynchronous operation completes within a specified `TimeSpan`. Unlike `Stopwatch`-based manual timing, the FluentAssertions form produces a human-readable failure message and integrates cleanly with the test runner's assertion pipeline. This pattern is appropriate for performance regression tests that guard against O(n²) accidental complexity regressions in hot paths.

```csharp
[Fact]
public void GetProductCatalog_With500Products_CompletesUnder50Ms()
{
    var repo = new InMemoryProductRepository(
        products: Enumerable.Range(1, 500)
            .Select(i => new Product { Id = $"SKU-{i}", Name = $"Product {i}" })
            .ToList());
    var service = new CatalogService(repo);

    Action act = () => service.GetAll(page: 1, pageSize: 20);

    act.ExecutionTime().Should().BeLessThan(50.Milliseconds(),
        because: "paginated catalogue fetch must stay under 50 ms SLA at 500 products");
}
```

**Tradeoff.** In-process timing asserts are JIT-sensitive on first runs; the initial invocation triggers JIT compilation that inflates the measured time. Warm up the method once before timing (`service.GetAll(1, 1)`) or mark the test `[Repeat(3)]` (NUnit) / run it after a warm-up call to reduce JIT noise. These tests are also sensitive to CI machine load — set a generous budget (3–5× the expected local time) to avoid flakiness on congested CI agents. [official]

---

### Pattern 189 — xUnit v3 `ITestOutputHelper` With Structured Logging Sink for Diagnostic Test Tracing [official]

xUnit v3's `ITestOutputHelper` can be wired as a Serilog or `Microsoft.Extensions.Logging` sink via adapter packages (`Serilog.Sinks.XUnit` or `MartinCostello.Logging.XUnit`). This routes all SUT log output into the test runner's output window, scoped to the individual test, making integration test failures self-diagnosing without requiring a separate log file or external trace viewer.

```csharp
public class InvoiceProcessingIntegrationTests(ITestOutputHelper output)
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task ProcessInvoice_ValidPdf_ExtractsLineItemsAndPersists()
    {
        var logger = new LoggerConfiguration()
            .MinimumLevel.Debug()
            .WriteTo.TestOutput(output, outputTemplate:
                "[{Timestamp:HH:mm:ss.fff} {Level:u3}] {SourceContext}: {Message}{NewLine}{Exception}")
            .CreateLogger();

        await using var scope = new ServiceCollection()
            .AddSingleton<ILogger>(logger)
            .AddSingleton<IInvoiceParser, PdfInvoiceParser>()
            .AddSingleton<IInvoiceRepository, InMemoryInvoiceRepository>()
            .BuildServiceProvider(validateScopes: true)
            .CreateAsyncScope();

        var processor = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IInvoiceParser>();
        var pdfBytes = await File.ReadAllBytesAsync("TestData/sample-invoice.pdf");

        var result = await processor.ParseAsync(pdfBytes);

        result.LineItems.Should().HaveCountGreaterThan(0);
        result.TotalAmount.Should().BePositive();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `ITestOutputHelper` output is only visible for failed tests by default in most CI reporters — passing tests produce no visible trace, which means diagnostic log lines silently vanish after a green run. When debugging a flaky test, temporarily add `output.WriteLine("[MARKER] reached assertion")` checkpoints; remove them before committing to avoid log noise in the CI test report. [official]

---

### Pattern 190 — Bogus `Faker<T>` for Domain-Aware Fake Data Generation in Integration Tests [community]

The `Bogus` library's `Faker<T>` class allows defining a reusable fake data factory for domain models with locale-aware, realistic values. Unlike `AutoFixture`, which generates structurally valid but semantically meaningless data (e.g., random GUIDs for `PostalCode`), `Bogus` produces values that pass domain validation rules (real UK postcodes, plausible dates of birth, valid ISBNs) — preventing false test failures caused by auto-generated data that violates business rules.

```csharp
public static class FakeData
{
    public static readonly Faker<Customer> CustomerFaker = new Faker<Customer>("en_GB")
        .RuleFor(c => c.Id, f => f.Random.Guid())
        .RuleFor(c => c.FirstName, f => f.Name.FirstName())
        .RuleFor(c => c.LastName, f => f.Name.LastName())
        .RuleFor(c => c.Email, (f, c) => f.Internet.Email(c.FirstName, c.LastName))
        .RuleFor(c => c.PostalCode, f => f.Address.ZipCode("??# #??").ToUpper())
        .RuleFor(c => c.DateOfBirth, f => f.Date.Past(50, DateTime.Today.AddYears(-18)))
        .RuleFor(c => c.IsVerified, f => f.Random.Bool(weight: 0.8f));

    public static Customer NewCustomer(Action<Customer>? overrides = null)
    {
        var customer = CustomerFaker.Generate();
        overrides?.Invoke(customer);
        return customer;
    }
}

// Usage in tests
[Fact]
public void RegisterCustomer_ValidDomainObject_PersistsSuccessfully()
{
    var customer = FakeData.NewCustomer(c => c.IsVerified = false);
    var repo = new InMemoryCustomerRepository();
    repo.Save(customer);
    repo.FindById(customer.Id).Should().BeEquivalentTo(customer);
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `Faker<T>` rules execute on every `.Generate()` call, making test data non-deterministic by default — two test runs produce different `PostalCode` values, which can mask bugs in code that only fails on certain patterns. Seed the `Faker` with a fixed value (`new Faker<T>().UseSeed(42)`) in tests that require reproducibility, and reserve unseeded fakers for property-based style tests that intentionally explore the input space. [community]

---

### Pattern 191 — `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing` With `IHostedService` Suppression for Faster Integration Test Startup [community]

`WebApplicationFactory<T>` starts all registered `IHostedService` implementations (background workers, health-check publishers, scheduled jobs) during test setup, often adding seconds to startup time and causing interference when background workers mutate shared test state. Removing specific hosted services via `ConfigureTestServices` scopes the integration test to only the components under test and eliminates non-deterministic background mutations.

```csharp
public class OrderApiFactory : WebApplicationFactory<Program>
{
    protected override void ConfigureWebHost(IWebHostBuilder builder)
    {
        builder.ConfigureTestServices(services =>
        {
            // Remove background workers that poll external systems
            services.RemoveAll<IHostedService>();

            // Re-register only the health-check hosted service if needed
            services.AddHostedService<HealthCheckService>();

            // Replace external dependencies with test doubles
            services.AddSingleton<IPaymentGateway, FakePaymentGateway>();
            services.AddSingleton<IEmailService, CapturedEmailService>();
        });

        builder.UseEnvironment("Testing");
    }
}

public class OrderApiTests(OrderApiFactory factory) 
    : IClassFixture<OrderApiFactory>
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task PostOrder_ValidPayload_Returns201WithOrderId()
    {
        var client = factory.CreateClient();
        var payload = new { ProductId = "SKU-1", Quantity = 2, Email = "test@example.com" };
        var response = await client.PostAsJsonAsync("/orders", payload);
        response.StatusCode.Should().Be(HttpStatusCode.Created);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Removing all `IHostedService` instances can mask bugs in background services that interact with the same database or message bus as the API under test — integration tests then cover a narrower system than production. Maintain a separate `FullStackIntegrationTests` collection that uses the full host for smoke tests, while using the hosted-service-suppressed factory for fast, targeted API contract tests. [community]

---

### Pattern 192 — NUnit 4 `Assume.That` for Precondition Guards That Mark Tests as Inconclusive [official]

NUnit's `Assume.That` evaluates a precondition and marks the test as `Inconclusive` (rather than failing) when the precondition is not met. This is the correct pattern for environment-dependent tests (e.g., tests that require a local Docker daemon, a licensed SDK, or a network connection) — `Inconclusive` distinguishes "could not run" from "ran and failed", preventing CI pipelines from treating unavailable infrastructure as a test failure.

```csharp
[Test]
public async Task ImportLargeDataset_LocalDockerRequired_CompletesWithin30s()
{
    // Guard: skip gracefully if Docker is not available in this environment
    Assume.That(
        await IsDockerAvailableAsync(),
        Is.True,
        "Docker daemon not available; test skipped on this agent");

    await using var container = new PostgreSqlBuilder()
        .WithImage("postgres:16-alpine")
        .Build();
    await container.StartAsync();

    var importer = new BulkDataImporter(container.GetConnectionString());
    var elapsed = await MeasureAsync(() =>
        importer.ImportAsync(LargeDatasetFixture.GetRows(count: 100_000)));

    Assert.That(elapsed, Is.LessThan(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)),
        "Bulk import exceeded 30-second SLA");
}

private static async Task<bool> IsDockerAvailableAsync()
{
    try { await DockerClient.DefaultLocalDockerEndpoint().PingAsync(); return true; }
    catch { return false; }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Teams that routinely see `Inconclusive` results may start ignoring them, treating them as effectively skipped — the signal degrades. Track `Inconclusive` counts in the CI summary and alert when they increase between builds to distinguish new environment-condition gaps from pre-existing ones. [official]

---

### Pattern 193 — Moq `Protected().Setup` for Testing Classes With `protected virtual` Members [official]

When the SUT contains a `protected virtual` method used for dependency inversion (e.g., `protected virtual HttpClient CreateClient()`), Moq's `Protected().Setup<TReturn>("MethodName", ...)` API creates a partial mock that overrides just that member. This avoids the need to extract an interface solely for testability when the protected-member pattern is already established in the codebase.

```csharp
public abstract class ExternalApiBase
{
    protected virtual HttpClient CreateHttpClient() =>
        new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://api.example.com") };

    public async Task<string> FetchDataAsync(string endpoint)
    {
        using var client = CreateHttpClient();
        return await client.GetStringAsync(endpoint);
    }
}

[Fact]
public async Task FetchData_HttpClientReturnsJson_DeserialisesProperly()
{
    var fakeHandler = new FakeHttpMessageHandler(
        new HttpResponseMessage(HttpStatusCode.OK)
        {
            Content = new StringContent("{\"id\":1,\"name\":\"Widget\"}")
        });

    var mockApi = new Mock<ExternalApiBase> { CallBase = true };
    mockApi
        .Protected()
        .Setup<HttpClient>("CreateHttpClient")
        .Returns(new HttpClient(fakeHandler)
            { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://api.example.com") });

    var result = await mockApi.Object.FetchDataAsync("/products/1");

    result.Should().Contain("\"name\":\"Widget\"");
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `Protected().Setup` uses string-based method names that are not refactor-safe — renaming `CreateHttpClient` compiles successfully but silently breaks the mock setup, causing tests to call the real method. Add a compiler-visible test helper (e.g., a public method on the test class that references the method name as a `nameof` expression in a comment) and include the setup in a nightly "mock integrity" test that at least verifies the protected method still exists via reflection. [official]

---

### Pattern 194 — `WireMock.Net` Stateful Scenario Mapping for Multi-Step HTTP Interaction Tests [community]

`WireMock.Net` supports stateful stub scenarios via `InScenario("name").WhenStateIs("state").WillSetStateTo("next-state")`, enabling integration tests to simulate multi-step HTTP protocols (OAuth token refresh, paginated APIs, retry-after flows). Unlike a single static stub, scenario mappings model the server's state machine, catching bugs in client retry and pagination logic that static stubs cannot detect.

```csharp
public class TokenRefreshIntegrationTests : IDisposable
{
    private readonly WireMockServer _server = WireMockServer.Start();

    public TokenRefreshIntegrationTests()
    {
        // First call returns 401, second call (after refresh) returns 200
        _server
            .Given(Request.Create().WithPath("/api/orders").UsingGet())
            .InScenario("token-expiry")
            .WhenStateIs(WireMockServer.NoState)
            .WillSetStateTo("token-expired")
            .RespondWith(Response.Create().WithStatusCode(401)
                .WithHeader("WWW-Authenticate", "Bearer error=\"invalid_token\""));

        _server
            .Given(Request.Create().WithPath("/api/orders").UsingGet())
            .InScenario("token-expiry")
            .WhenStateIs("token-expired")
            .RespondWith(Response.Create().WithStatusCode(200)
                .WithBodyAsJson(new { orders = new[] { new { id = "ORD-1" } } }));

        _server
            .Given(Request.Create().WithPath("/oauth/token").UsingPost())
            .RespondWith(Response.Create().WithStatusCode(200)
                .WithBodyAsJson(new { access_token = "new-token-abc", expires_in = 3600 }));
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task GetOrders_ExpiredToken_AutoRefreshesAndReturnsData()
    {
        var client = new OrderApiClient(new Uri(_server.Urls[0]));
        var orders = await client.GetOrdersAsync();
        orders.Should().ContainSingle(o => o.Id == "ORD-1");
    }

    public void Dispose() => _server.Stop();
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Scenario state is global to the `WireMockServer` instance — if tests run in parallel, one test's state transition can corrupt another's. Always create a fresh `WireMockServer` per test class (not per test, due to port allocation cost) and use `_server.Reset()` in `[TearDown]` / `Dispose` to clear scenario state between tests within the same class. [community]

---

### Pattern 195 — `Respawn` Database Checkpoint for Blazing-Fast Integration Test Isolation Without Container Restart [community]

`Respawn` (by Jimmy Bogard) creates a database checkpoint after initial schema and seed setup, then resets the database to that checkpoint between tests by generating a targeted `DELETE` statement that respects foreign-key ordering — much faster than dropping/recreating the schema or restarting a container. This enables hundreds of database integration tests to run in seconds rather than minutes.

```csharp
public class DatabaseFixture : IAsyncLifetime
{
    public IDbConnection Connection { get; private set; } = null!;
    private Respawner _respawner = null!;

    public async Task InitializeAsync()
    {
        Connection = new NpgsqlConnection(
            "Host=localhost;Database=test_orders;Username=test;Password=test");
        await ((NpgsqlConnection)Connection).OpenAsync();

        // Apply migrations once
        await Migrator.ApplyAsync(Connection);

        // Seed reference data that must survive resets
        await SeedReferenceDataAsync(Connection);

        // Create checkpoint AFTER seeding reference data
        _respawner = await Respawner.CreateAsync(
            (NpgsqlConnection)Connection,
            new RespawnerOptions
            {
                DbAdapter = DbAdapter.Postgres,
                TablesToIgnore = new[] { new Table("countries"), new Table("currencies") }
            });
    }

    public async Task ResetAsync() => await _respawner.ResetAsync(
        (NpgsqlConnection)Connection);

    public async Task DisposeAsync() => await Connection.DisposeAsync();
}

public class OrderRepositoryTests(DatabaseFixture db)
    : IClassFixture<DatabaseFixture>
{
    public async Task InitializeAsync() => await db.ResetAsync();

    [Fact]
    public async Task Save_NewOrder_PersistsAndRetrievesById()
    {
        var repo = new OrderRepository(db.Connection);
        var order = new Order { Id = "ORD-001", Amount = 150m, Status = "Pending" };
        await repo.SaveAsync(order);
        var found = await repo.FindByIdAsync("ORD-001");
        found.Should().BeEquivalentTo(order);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `Respawn` issues `DELETE` statements without truncating sequences — auto-increment identity columns continue from where they left off between resets, so tests that assert on specific generated IDs (e.g., `Id == 1`) will fail after the first reset. Always assert on the returned entity rather than on assumed identity values; use `TRUNCATE ... RESTART IDENTITY` explicitly when sequence reset is required and `Respawn`'s DELETE approach is insufficient. [community]

---

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 52

**xUnit v3 `[ClassData]` source classes must be `public` — an `internal` or `private` data class compiles without warning but causes all theory cases to be reported as "No data found" at discovery time, silently producing zero test runs rather than a compile error [community]** — A developer defines `class MyTheoryData : TheoryData<int, string>` without an access modifier (defaulting to `internal`) inside the test namespace. Test Explorer shows the `[Theory]` method with a green icon but zero cases; the test is reported as passed with 0 iterations. WHY it causes problems: the test appears to pass in CI, providing false green confidence — the entire data set is never exercised. Fix: always mark `[ClassData]` source classes as `public`, and add a companion test that asserts `new MyTheoryData().Count > 0` to catch empty data sources.

**Moq `It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()` in a `Setup` does not distinguish between a cancelled and a non-cancelled token — if the SUT is expected to propagate a `CancellationToken` from the caller but passes `CancellationToken.None` instead, the mock setup matches and the test passes, masking the propagation bug [community]** — A developer sets up `mock.Setup(s => s.FetchAsync(It.IsAny<string>(), It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()))` and verifies only the return value. The SUT passes `CancellationToken.None` instead of the token from the caller. The test passes. WHY it causes problems: in production, operations that should be cancellable are not — long-running HTTP calls ignore the user-initiated cancellation. Fix: use a `CancellationTokenSource` in the test, pass `cts.Token` to the SUT, cancel it mid-flight, and assert that the SUT's call propagates cancellation via `It.Is<CancellationToken>(t => !t.Equals(CancellationToken.None))` or by asserting `OperationCanceledException` is thrown.

**FluentAssertions `BeEquivalentTo` with `ExcludingMissingMembers()` on a DTO-to-domain mapping test hides new properties added to the domain model that are missing from the DTO — the option silently skips unmatched expected properties rather than failing [community]** — A team uses `result.Should().BeEquivalentTo(dto, opts => opts.ExcludingMissingMembers())` to assert a domain-to-DTO mapping. A developer adds `ShippingAddress` to the domain `Order` class but forgets to add it to `OrderDto`. The test continues to pass because the missing member is excluded. WHY it causes problems: the new field is never tested for correct mapping and silently returns `null` in the API response. Fix: avoid `ExcludingMissingMembers()` in mapping tests; instead, explicitly exclude known structural differences with `.Excluding(o => o.InternalAuditLog)` so that any new property omission causes an immediate compilation or assertion failure.

**Testcontainers.NET containers started with `await container.StartAsync()` inside a `[OneTimeSetUp]` without a corresponding `await container.DisposeAsync()` in `[OneTimeTearDown]` leave orphaned Docker containers running on the build agent after a test run crash — because the container lifecycle is not tied to process exit by default [community]** — A build agent accumulates dozens of postgres containers over several failing CI builds. Each container holds an OS-assigned port; eventually the port range is exhausted and new containers fail to start with `bind: address already in use`. WHY it causes problems: the failure manifests as an infrastructure error rather than a test failure, causing the team to investigate Docker daemon health rather than the test lifecycle. Fix: always implement `[OneTimeTearDown]` with `await container.DisposeAsync()`, and add the `TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=false` environment variable to CI to ensure the Ryuk reaper container cleans up orphaned resources even on process crash.

**NUnit 4 `[Parallelizable(ParallelScope.All)]` applied to a test class that writes to `TestContext.CurrentContext.TestDirectory` causes intermittent `DirectoryNotFoundException` — parallel tests from different classes resolve `TestDirectory` to the same path and one test's cleanup deletes the directory while another is writing to it [community]** — A suite of file-processing integration tests each create a temporary subdirectory under `TestContext.CurrentContext.TestDirectory`, process files, then delete the subdirectory in `[TearDown]`. Under `ParallelScope.All`, two tests' `[TearDown]` methods race: test A's teardown deletes the shared root directory milliseconds before test B tries to write its output file into a subdirectory of it. WHY it causes problems: the failure is intermittent and machine-speed-dependent, passing on developer machines (lower parallelism) but failing on CI agents (8-core agents run more threads simultaneously). Fix: use `Path.Combine(TestContext.CurrentContext.TestDirectory, TestContext.CurrentContext.Test.ID)` to create per-test subdirectories that are guaranteed unique across parallel runners, and verify the directory does not exist before creating it.

---

### Anti-Patterns Quick Reference — Cycle 52 Additions

| Anti-Pattern | Why It's Harmful | What to Do Instead |
|---|---|---|
| `[ClassData]` source class with default (`internal`) access modifier | Theory produces zero test cases silently; test appears to pass with no iterations | Always mark `[ClassData]` source classes `public`; add a count assertion test |
| `It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()` in Moq setup when token propagation matters | Passes even when SUT passes `CancellationToken.None`, hiding cancellation bugs | Use `It.Is<CancellationToken>(t => !t.Equals(CancellationToken.None))` or assert `OperationCanceledException` |
| `BeEquivalentTo` with `ExcludingMissingMembers()` in mapping tests | New domain properties missing from DTOs are silently excluded; mapping gaps go undetected | Use explicit `.Excluding(o => o.KnownIgnoredProp)` instead; never use `ExcludingMissingMembers` in mapping assertions |
| Testcontainers `StartAsync` without matching `DisposeAsync` in teardown | Orphaned Docker containers accumulate on CI agents; port exhaustion causes infrastructure failures | Always implement `[OneTimeTearDown]` with `DisposeAsync`; enable Ryuk reaper (`TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=false`) |
| `[Parallelizable(ParallelScope.All)]` with shared `TestDirectory` writes | Parallel teardown races cause intermittent `DirectoryNotFoundException` on multi-core CI agents | Use `TestContext.CurrentContext.Test.ID` as a per-test subdirectory suffix for isolation |
| `Faker<T>` with no seed in reproducibility-sensitive tests | Non-deterministic data masks bugs that only manifest for specific value patterns | Use `.UseSeed(n)` for reproducible runs; reserve unseeded fakers for exploratory property-based tests |

## Cycle 53 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 196 — xUnit v3 `IAsyncLifetime` on Test Classes for Fully Async Setup and Teardown [official]

xUnit v3 ships a dedicated `IAsyncLifetime` interface with `InitializeAsync()` and `DisposeAsync()` methods that replace constructor-based side-effects for anything that requires `await`. Implementing the interface on the test class eliminates the `Task.Run(async () => ...)` antipattern that previously crept into synchronous constructors when async resource setup was needed.

```csharp
using Xunit;

public class OrderServiceTests : IAsyncLifetime
{
    private OrderService _service = null!;
    private InMemoryEventBus _bus = null!;

    public async Task InitializeAsync()
    {
        _bus = new InMemoryEventBus();
        _service = new OrderService(_bus);
        await _service.WarmUpCacheAsync(); // legitimately async
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task PlaceOrder_PublishesOrderPlacedEvent()
    {
        var order = new Order { Id = "ORD-1", Amount = 99m };
        await _service.PlaceAsync(order);
        _bus.Published.Should().ContainSingle(e => e is OrderPlacedEvent);
    }

    public async Task DisposeAsync()
    {
        await _service.DisposeAsync();
        await _bus.DisposeAsync();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `IAsyncLifetime` runs once per test instance (xUnit creates a new instance per test by default), so each test pays the full setup cost. For expensive operations shared across tests, combine with `IClassFixture<T>` where the fixture itself implements `IAsyncLifetime`. [official]

---

### Pattern 197 — NUnit 4 `Assert.ThrowsAsync<T>` With Fluent `With.Message` Constraint for Exception Detail Assertions [official]

NUnit 4 exposes `Assert.ThrowsAsync<T>` that returns the caught exception, enabling full constraint application on the exception object after the throw assertion. This is more expressive than a bare `ThrowsAsync` check and avoids wrapping `try/catch` in test code.

```csharp
using NUnit.Framework;

[TestFixture]
public class PaymentGatewayTests
{
    private PaymentGateway _gateway = null!;

    [SetUp]
    public void SetUp() => _gateway = new PaymentGateway(new FakeHttpClient());

    [Test]
    public async Task Charge_WithExpiredCard_ThrowsPaymentExceptionWithCode()
    {
        var ex = Assert.ThrowsAsync<PaymentException>(
            async () => await _gateway.ChargeAsync("card_expired", 50m));

        Assert.That(ex, Is.Not.Null);
        Assert.That(ex!.ErrorCode, Is.EqualTo("card_expired"));
        Assert.That(ex.Message, Does.Contain("expired").IgnoreCase);
        Assert.That(ex.RetryAfter, Is.Null,
            "Expired-card errors are not retriable");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `Assert.ThrowsAsync<T>` unwraps `AggregateException` one level automatically when the awaited delegate wraps the exception — but it does *not* recursively unwrap nested aggregates. If the SUT wraps exceptions multiple levels deep (e.g., `Task.WhenAll` over multiple faulted tasks), use `Assert.ThrowsAsync<AggregateException>` and inspect `.InnerExceptions` directly. [official]

---

### Pattern 198 — MSTest v3 `[TestClass]` With `[AssemblyInitialize]` and `AssemblyCleanup` for One-Time Test Assembly Bootstrapping [official]

MSTest v3 supports static `[AssemblyInitialize]` and `[AssemblyCleanup]` methods that run exactly once per test assembly, making them the right place to start heavyweight shared infrastructure (e.g., a single `WebApplicationFactory` or a Docker network) that is too costly to recreate per class.

```csharp
using Microsoft.VisualStudio.TestTools.UnitTesting;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;

[TestClass]
public static class TestAssemblySetup
{
    public static WebApplicationFactory<Program> Factory { get; private set; } = null!;
    public static HttpClient Client { get; private set; } = null!;

    [AssemblyInitialize]
    public static void Init(TestContext ctx)
    {
        Factory = new WebApplicationFactory<Program>()
            .WithWebHostBuilder(b =>
                b.UseEnvironment("Testing"));
        Client = Factory.CreateClient();
    }

    [AssemblyCleanup]
    public static void Cleanup()
    {
        Client.Dispose();
        Factory.Dispose();
    }
}

[TestClass]
public class ProductApiTests
{
    [TestMethod]
    public async Task GetProducts_Returns200()
    {
        var resp = await TestAssemblySetup.Client.GetAsync("/api/products");
        resp.StatusCode.Should().Be(HttpStatusCode.OK);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Assembly-scoped state is global — any test that mutates the factory's DI container or shared `HttpClient` headers affects all subsequent tests in the run. Prefer `[ClassInitialize]` for mutating setups; reserve `[AssemblyInitialize]` for read-only shared infrastructure. MSTest does not guarantee the order in which `[AssemblyInitialize]` methods across multiple `[TestClass]`-annotated setup classes run; keep only one per assembly. [official]

---

### Pattern 199 — FluentAssertions `HaveCount` + `SatisfyRespectively` Chained on Collections for Positional Element Assertions [official]

FluentAssertions' `SatisfyRespectively` accepts one assertion delegate per expected element and enforces both count and per-element shape in a single readable expression. Chaining `.HaveCount` before it makes the failure message explicit about whether the count or an element's shape was wrong.

```csharp
using FluentAssertions;

[Fact]
public void GetSortedOrders_ReturnsThreeOrdersInAscendingAmountOrder()
{
    var service = new OrderService(SeedOrders());

    var orders = service.GetSortedByAmount();

    orders.Should()
        .HaveCount(3)
        .And.SatisfyRespectively(
            first =>
            {
                first.Id.Should().Be("ORD-001");
                first.Amount.Should().Be(25m);
            },
            second =>
            {
                second.Id.Should().Be("ORD-002");
                second.Amount.Should().Be(75m);
            },
            third =>
            {
                third.Id.Should().Be("ORD-003");
                third.Amount.Should().BeGreaterThan(100m);
            });
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `SatisfyRespectively` is strictly positional — element ordering matters. If the SUT may return results in any valid order (e.g., a database query without `ORDER BY`), use `Satisfy(delegates)` (unordered) or `BeEquivalentTo(expected)` with `ComparingByMembers` instead to avoid order-sensitive false failures. [official]

---

### Pattern 200 — `Moq` `SetupSequence` for Simulating Transient Failures and Retry Behaviour [official]

`SetupSequence<T>` on a Moq mock configures successive return values or thrown exceptions for repeated calls to the same method, enabling accurate simulation of transient failure-then-success scenarios required for testing retry logic in Polly pipelines or custom retry loops.

```csharp
using Moq;
using FluentAssertions;

[Fact]
public async Task FetchUser_RetriesToleratesOneTransientFailure()
{
    var mockRepo = new Mock<IUserRepository>();
    mockRepo
        .SetupSequence(r => r.FindByIdAsync(It.IsAny<string>(),
                                            It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()))
        .ThrowsAsync(new TransientException("timeout"))  // call 1 → throw
        .ReturnsAsync(new User { Id = "U1", Name = "Alice" }); // call 2 → succeed

    var pipeline = ResiliencePipelineBuilder.New()
        .AddRetry(new RetryStrategyOptions
        {
            MaxRetryAttempts = 2,
            Delay = TimeSpan.Zero
        })
        .Build();

    var user = await pipeline.ExecuteAsync(
        async ct => await mockRepo.Object.FindByIdAsync("U1", ct));

    user.Name.Should().Be("Alice");
    mockRepo.Verify(r => r.FindByIdAsync("U1", It.IsAny<CancellationToken>()),
        Times.Exactly(2));
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Once all configured responses in a `SetupSequence` are consumed, subsequent calls fall through to the default mock behaviour (null/default for `MockBehavior.Loose`, exception for `MockBehavior.Strict`). Always set up one more response than the maximum expected call count, or verify the exact call count after execution, to catch over-retry bugs where the SUT retries more than intended. [official]

---

### Pattern 201 — Testcontainers.NET `DockerfileBuilder` for Custom Application Container Tests [official]

Testcontainers.NET `ImageFromDockerfileBuilder` builds a Docker image from a local `Dockerfile` at test startup, enabling full integration tests against the real production container image rather than a pre-built registry tag. This guarantees the Dockerfile being tested matches what ships to production.

```csharp
using DotNet.Testcontainers.Builders;
using DotNet.Testcontainers.Containers;

public class AppContainerTests : IAsyncLifetime
{
    private IContainer _appContainer = null!;

    public async Task InitializeAsync()
    {
        var image = await new ImageFromDockerfileBuilder()
            .WithDockerfileDirectory(CommonDirectoryPath.GetSolutionDirectory(), string.Empty)
            .WithDockerfile("src/MyApi/Dockerfile")
            .WithName("myapi-test:latest")
            .WithDeleteIfExists(true)
            .BuildAsync();

        _appContainer = new ContainerBuilder()
            .WithImage(image)
            .WithPortBinding(8080, true)
            .WithEnvironment("ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT", "Testing")
            .WithWaitStrategy(Wait.ForUnixContainer()
                .UntilHttpRequestIsSucceeded(r => r.ForPort(8080).ForPath("/health")))
            .Build();

        await _appContainer.StartAsync();
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task HealthEndpoint_ReturnsHealthy()
    {
        var host = _appContainer.Hostname;
        var port = _appContainer.GetMappedPublicPort(8080);
        var client = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri($"http://{host}:{port}") };
        var resp = await client.GetAsync("/health");
        resp.IsSuccessStatusCode.Should().BeTrue();
    }

    public async Task DisposeAsync() => await _appContainer.DisposeAsync();
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Building the image from the `Dockerfile` on every test run adds significant startup time (often 30–120 seconds for a multi-stage build). Use `WithDeleteIfExists(false)` and tag the image consistently so Docker layer caching is leveraged on repeat runs; clean the image explicitly in nightly CI to avoid stale cache divergence. [official]

---

### Pattern 202 — `Microsoft.Extensions.Http` `AddHttpClient` With `IHttpClientFactory` and a `MockHttpMessageHandler` for Isolated HTTP Call Testing [official]

Rather than constructing `HttpClient` directly in tests, register a named or typed client via `AddHttpClient` in a `ServiceCollection` and swap the `HttpMessageHandler` with a `MockHttpMessageHandler` (from `RichardSzalay.MockHttp`). This mirrors the production DI registration and exercises the delegating handler pipeline.

```csharp
using RichardSzalay.MockHttp;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using FluentAssertions;

[Fact]
public async Task GitHubClient_GetUser_DeserializesLoginCorrectly()
{
    var mockHttp = new MockHttpMessageHandler();
    mockHttp
        .When("https://api.github.com/users/octocat")
        .Respond("application/json",
            """{"login":"octocat","id":1}""");

    var services = new ServiceCollection();
    services
        .AddHttpClient<GitHubClient>(c =>
            c.BaseAddress = new Uri("https://api.github.com/"))
        .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => mockHttp);

    var provider = services.BuildServiceProvider();
    var client = provider.GetRequiredService<GitHubClient>();

    var user = await client.GetUserAsync("octocat");

    user.Login.Should().Be("octocat");
    mockHttp.VerifyNoOutstandingExpectation();
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `MockHttpMessageHandler` replaces the primary handler but not delegating handlers added via `.AddHttpMessageHandler<T>()` — those are still invoked in the pipeline. If you need to test that a retry or logging delegating handler fires, keep the real delegating handlers registered and only replace the innermost primary handler. [official]

---

### Pattern 203 — NUnit 4 `[TestCase]` With `TestName` and `Category` for Filtered, Self-Documenting Parameterised Tests [official]

NUnit 4 `[TestCase]` accepts `TestName` and `Category` named parameters inline, allowing each parameterised case to carry a human-readable display name and to belong to a category that can be targeted with `--where "cat == smoke"` in the CLI, without a separate `[Category]` attribute.

```csharp
using NUnit.Framework;

[TestFixture]
public class VatCalculatorTests
{
    [TestCase(100m, "GB", 20m,
        TestName = "UK standard rate 20%",
        Category = "smoke")]
    [TestCase(100m, "DE", 19m,
        TestName = "Germany standard rate 19%",
        Category = "smoke")]
    [TestCase(100m, "ZZ", 0m,
        TestName = "Unknown country zero-rated",
        Category = "edge-case")]
    public void Calculate_ReturnsCorrectVat(
        decimal net, string country, decimal expectedVat)
    {
        var calculator = new VatCalculator();
        var vat = calculator.Calculate(net, country);
        Assert.That(vat, Is.EqualTo(expectedVat));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Inline `Category` on `[TestCase]` attributes works for filtering individual cases but does not surface as a category in all test runners — JetBrains Rider displays it correctly, Visual Studio Test Explorer groups only by the `[Category]` attribute applied to the method. For VS Test Explorer category filtering, apply a separate `[Category]` attribute at the method level and use `TestName` only for display. [official]

---

### Pattern 204 — `AutoFixture` `[AutoData]` With `ICustomization` Interface for Reusable Domain Object Creation Strategies [community]

AutoFixture's `[AutoData]` attribute can accept a custom `IFixture` configurator via a derived attribute that applies domain-specific customizations — such as constraining `decimal` ranges, configuring value objects, or overriding string generation — enabling consistent, realistic test data across the whole test project without `fixture.Customize` boilerplate in every test.

```csharp
using AutoFixture;
using AutoFixture.Xunit2;

// Domain customization: positive amounts, short strings, valid status
public class DomainCustomization : ICustomization
{
    public void Customize(IFixture fixture)
    {
        fixture.Customize<decimal>(c => c.FromFactory(() =>
            Math.Round((decimal)(new Random().NextDouble() * 999 + 1), 2)));
        fixture.Customize<Order>(c => c
            .With(o => o.Status, "Pending")
            .With(o => o.Amount, fixture.Create<decimal>())
            .Without(o => o.CancelledAt));
    }
}

public class AutoDomainDataAttribute : AutoDataAttribute
{
    public AutoDomainDataAttribute()
        : base(() => new Fixture().Customize(new DomainCustomization())) { }
}

public class OrderServiceTests
{
    [Theory, AutoDomainData]
    public void ApplyDiscount_ReducesAmountByPercentage(Order order)
    {
        var original = order.Amount;
        order.ApplyDiscount(10m); // 10%
        order.Amount.Should().Be(Math.Round(original * 0.9m, 2));
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** A broad `ICustomization` that overrides too many types creates invisible coupling — tests that rely on specific values for a type will silently receive customized values instead. Document the customization contract clearly, and prefer named `[InlineAutoData]` or `[MemberAutoData]` for tests where specific boundary values matter. [community]

---

### Pattern 205 — `WebApplicationFactory` With `ReplaceService<T>` Extension for Clean Per-Test Dependency Overrides [official]

ASP.NET Core 8+ `WebApplicationFactory` supports a concise `Services.Replace` (via `ServiceDescriptor`) pattern for swapping a single registered service with a test double without rebuilding the entire DI container. A helper extension method `ReplaceService<TService, TImpl>` makes this idiomatic in test code.

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;

public static class WebApplicationFactoryExtensions
{
    public static WebApplicationFactory<TEntryPoint> WithService<TService, TImpl>(
        this WebApplicationFactory<TEntryPoint> factory,
        TImpl implementation)
        where TEntryPoint : class
        where TImpl : class, TService
        where TService : class
    {
        return factory.WithWebHostBuilder(builder =>
            builder.ConfigureServices(services =>
            {
                services.Remove(
                    services.Single(d => d.ServiceType == typeof(TService)));
                services.AddSingleton<TService>(implementation);
            }));
    }
}

public class NotificationApiTests(WebApplicationFactory<Program> factory)
    : IClassFixture<WebApplicationFactory<Program>>
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task SendNotification_CallsEmailSender()
    {
        var fakeEmailSender = new FakeEmailSender();
        var client = factory
            .WithService<IEmailSender, FakeEmailSender>(fakeEmailSender)
            .CreateClient();

        await client.PostAsJsonAsync("/api/notify",
            new { UserId = "U1", Message = "Hello" });

        fakeEmailSender.SentMessages.Should().ContainSingle(
            m => m.UserId == "U1");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** Each call to `WithWebHostBuilder` creates a new `WebApplicationFactory` child scope and rebuilds the host — avoid calling it inside a loop for bulk test parameterisation. For tests that only differ in request data, share one factory override and vary the HTTP request body instead. [official]

---

### Pattern 206 — `ArchUnitNET` Architecture Rule Enforcement for Dependency Direction Violations in CI [community]

ArchUnitNET (the .NET port of ArchUnit) enables executable architecture rules that assert layer dependencies flow in one direction, namespaces do not reference each other incorrectly, and public types in core assemblies do not reference infrastructure types. These rules run as ordinary test methods and fail the build immediately when a violation is introduced.

```csharp
using ArchUnitNET.Domain;
using ArchUnitNET.Fluent;
using ArchUnitNET.Loader;
using ArchUnitNET.xUnit;
using Xunit;
using static ArchUnitNET.Fluent.ArchRuleDefinition;

public class ArchitectureTests
{
    private static readonly Architecture Architecture =
        new ArchLoader()
            .LoadAssemblies(
                typeof(Order).Assembly,        // Domain
                typeof(OrderRepository).Assembly, // Infrastructure
                typeof(OrderController).Assembly) // Api
            .Build();

    [Fact]
    public void Domain_ShouldNotDependOnInfrastructure()
    {
        var domainLayer = Types()
            .That().ResideInNamespace("MyApp.Domain", true);
        var infraLayer = Types()
            .That().ResideInNamespace("MyApp.Infrastructure", true);

        var rule = domainLayer
            .Should().NotDependOnAny(infraLayer)
            .Because("Domain must remain persistence-ignorant");

        rule.Check(Architecture);
    }

    [Fact]
    public void Application_ShouldNotReferenceApiLayer()
    {
        var appLayer = Types().That().ResideInNamespace("MyApp.Application", true);
        var apiLayer = Types().That().ResideInNamespace("MyApp.Api", true);

        Classes().That().Are(appLayer)
            .Should().NotDependOnAny(apiLayer)
            .Because("Application use-cases must be framework-agnostic")
            .Check(Architecture);
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** ArchUnitNET loads assemblies via reflection at test initialisation, which adds a noticeable startup cost (typically 2–5 seconds per assembly). Extract the `Architecture` object as a static field shared across all architecture test methods in the class, and use `IClassFixture<ArchitectureFixture>` for xUnit or `[OneTimeSetUp]` for NUnit to pay the load cost once. [community]

---

### Pattern 207 — `.NET 8+ `TimeProvider` Injection for Deterministic Date and Time Tests Without System Clock [official]

`System.TimeProvider` (introduced in .NET 8) is the official abstraction for `DateTime.UtcNow`, `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`, and timer creation. Injecting `TimeProvider` into production services and using `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing.FakeTimeProvider` in tests removes all `DateTime.Now` non-determinism without wrapping the system clock in a custom interface.

```csharp
using Microsoft.Extensions.Time.Testing;
using FluentAssertions;

public class SubscriptionExpiryServiceTests
{
    [Fact]
    public void IsExpired_ReturnsTrue_WhenCurrentTimeIsAfterExpiryDate()
    {
        var fakeTime = new FakeTimeProvider();
        fakeTime.SetUtcNow(new DateTimeOffset(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero));

        var service = new SubscriptionExpiryService(fakeTime);
        var sub = new Subscription
        {
            ExpiresAt = new DateTimeOffset(2025, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59, TimeSpan.Zero)
        };

        service.IsExpired(sub).Should().BeTrue();
    }

    [Fact]
    public void GracePeriod_ExpiresAfter48Hours()
    {
        var fakeTime = new FakeTimeProvider();
        var start = new DateTimeOffset(2026, 3, 1, 12, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero);
        fakeTime.SetUtcNow(start);

        var service = new SubscriptionExpiryService(fakeTime);
        var sub = new Subscription { ExpiresAt = start };

        service.IsInGracePeriod(sub).Should().BeTrue("grace period just started");

        fakeTime.Advance(TimeSpan.FromHours(48).Add(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1)));

        service.IsInGracePeriod(sub).Should().BeFalse("grace period has elapsed");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `FakeTimeProvider` does not automatically advance time — calling `Advance(TimeSpan)` is always explicit. Code that spawns `Task.Delay` or `PeriodicTimer` internally will not automatically complete when `fakeTime.Advance` is called unless the timer was created via the same `TimeProvider` instance. Pass `timeProvider.CreateTimer(...)` in production code, not `Task.Delay`, to make timer-based logic fully testable. [official]

---

### Pattern 208 — xUnit v3 `[MemberData]` With `TheoryDataRow` `Skip` Property for Conditional Test Case Exclusion [official]

xUnit v3 `TheoryDataRow<T>` supports a `.Skip` property that conditionally excludes individual data-driven cases at discovery time without removing them from the source collection. This enables platform-conditional or environment-conditional skipping inline in the data source, keeping skipped cases visible in test results rather than silently absent.

```csharp
using Xunit;

public class PlatformTests
{
    public static TheoryData<TheoryDataRow<string, bool>> PlatformCases => new()
    {
        new TheoryDataRow<string, bool>("Windows", true)
        {
            Skip = OperatingSystem.IsLinux()
                ? "Windows-only path separator test"
                : null
        },
        new TheoryDataRow<string, bool>("Linux", false)
        {
            Skip = OperatingSystem.IsWindows()
                ? "Linux-only symlink test"
                : null
        },
        new TheoryDataRow<string, bool>("CrossPlatform", true)
        // No Skip — always runs
    };

    [Theory]
    [MemberData(nameof(PlatformCases))]
    public void FileSystem_PathHandling_IsCorrect(string scenario, bool expectAbsolute)
    {
        var path = FileSystemHelper.NormalizePath(scenario);
        Path.IsPathRooted(path).Should().Be(expectAbsolute,
            because: $"scenario '{scenario}' expected rooted={expectAbsolute}");
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `TheoryDataRow.Skip` is evaluated at discovery time, not execution time — the condition runs in the process that loads the test assembly (which may be `dotnet test` CLI, VS Test Explorer, or Rider's test runner). Avoid using `Skip` conditions that depend on runtime state unavailable at discovery (e.g., database connectivity); use `Assume.That` (NUnit) or `Skip.If` (xUnit) at the start of the test body for runtime guards instead. [official]

---

### Pattern 209 — NSubstitute `When...Do` for Void Methods and Side-Effect Injection in Mocks [official]

NSubstitute's `When(sub => sub.Method()).Do(callInfo => ...)` syntax configures callbacks on `void`-returning methods or on calls that need to produce observable side effects beyond the return value, such as mutating a captured collection, setting an `out` parameter, or raising an event.

```csharp
using NSubstitute;
using FluentAssertions;

[Fact]
public void OrderProcessor_OnSuccess_RaisesCompletedEvent()
{
    var notifier = Substitute.For<IOrderNotifier>();
    var publishedEvents = new List<string>();

    notifier
        .When(n => n.Notify(Arg.Any<string>()))
        .Do(callInfo =>
        {
            var orderId = callInfo.Arg<string>();
            publishedEvents.Add($"notified:{orderId}");
        });

    var processor = new OrderProcessor(notifier);
    processor.Process(new Order { Id = "ORD-42", Amount = 100m });

    publishedEvents.Should().ContainSingle()
        .Which.Should().Be("notified:ORD-42");
    notifier.Received(1).Notify("ORD-42");
}
```

**Tradeoff.** `When...Do` callbacks execute synchronously in the calling thread — if the callback throws, the exception propagates to the SUT as if the dependency threw, potentially masking the actual test intent. Keep `Do` callbacks simple (capture, increment, append) and use `Returns(x => ...)` for methods with return values rather than mixing `Do` and return configuration on the same call. [official]

---

### Pattern 210 — `TUnit` Parallel-First Test Framework With Source-Generated Parallelism for .NET 8+ [community]

TUnit is a modern, source-generator-based test framework for .NET 8+ that generates test registration code at compile time instead of using reflection at runtime. Its default execution mode is parallel-first, tests are composable with `[DependsOn]` ordering constraints, and the framework supports `ClassConstructor<T>` for DI-friendly class instantiation — filling gaps that xUnit and NUnit address with workarounds.

```csharp
using TUnit.Core;
using TUnit.Assertions;
using TUnit.Assertions.Extensions;

[ClassConstructor<TestServiceProvider>]
public class ProductServiceTUnitTests(ProductService svc)
{
    [Test]
    [Arguments(1, "Widget")]
    [Arguments(2, "Gadget")]
    public async Task GetById_ReturnsMatchingProduct(int id, string expectedName)
    {
        var product = await svc.GetByIdAsync(id);
        await Assert.That(product.Name).IsEqualTo(expectedName);
    }

    [Test]
    [DependsOn(nameof(GetById_ReturnsMatchingProduct))]
    public async Task Delete_AfterGet_RemovesProduct()
    {
        await svc.DeleteAsync(1);
        var product = await svc.GetByIdAsync(1);
        await Assert.That(product).IsNull();
    }
}
```

**Tradeoff.** TUnit is production-quality but younger than xUnit/NUnit, meaning IDE support (especially in Visual Studio 2022 pre-17.10) may require manual adapter installation, and the NuGet ecosystem of community extensions (AutoFixture, Bogus, Moq integrations) targets xUnit/NUnit data attribute conventions. Evaluate TUnit for greenfield high-parallelism scenarios; for existing projects, migration cost versus parallel performance gains must be weighed carefully. [community]

---

### Community Gotchas — Cycle 53

**Gotcha 1 — xUnit v3 `IAsyncLifetime.DisposeAsync` is NOT called if `InitializeAsync` throws — leaving partially initialised resources (e.g., a started-but-not-registered container) orphaned with no cleanup path [community]** — A team wraps Testcontainers startup in `IAsyncLifetime.InitializeAsync` and creates a `CancellationTokenSource` first, starts the container second, then awaits an HTTP health probe third. If the health probe times out, `InitializeAsync` throws and `DisposeAsync` is never called — the container keeps running. WHY it causes problems: on a shared CI agent running many parallel test workers, orphaned containers accumulate rapidly, exhaust available ports, and cause the next test run to fail with `bind: address already in use` rather than a clear timeout error. Fix: use a `try/finally` block within `InitializeAsync` to call `container.DisposeAsync()` on failure paths, or register cleanup in the fixture constructor using `try/catch` around the startup await.

**Gotcha 2 — Moq `SetupSequence` silently falls back to the mock's default behaviour after all configured responses are consumed — if a retry policy calls the dependency one more time than expected, `SetupSequence` returns `default(T)` for Loose mocks rather than throwing, causing the test to pass when it should fail [community]** — A developer configures `SetupSequence` with two responses (one throw, one success) to test a two-attempt retry. A misconfigured Polly policy actually retries three times; the third call returns `null` (default for `MockBehavior.Loose`), the SUT null-dereferences, and the test fails with a `NullReferenceException` in the SUT code rather than a clear assertion failure. WHY it causes problems: the failure message points at the SUT's null-deref line, not at the retry misconfiguration, sending the developer to debug the wrong layer. Fix: always follow a `SetupSequence` with a `Verify(Times.Exactly(n))` call to assert the expected number of calls, and prefer `MockBehavior.Strict` so unexpected extra calls throw immediately with a meaningful message.

**Gotcha 3 — FluentAssertions `BeEquivalentTo` does NOT compare `IEnumerable<T>` properties by element order by default — two collections in reverse order are considered equivalent, masking ordering bugs in sort operations [community]** — A developer asserts `result.Should().BeEquivalentTo(expected)` on a domain object that contains a `List<LineItem>` property. The `List<LineItem>` on the expected object is sorted by `Sequence` ascending; the SUT returns them in reverse order. The assertion passes because `BeEquivalentTo` treats collections as bags by default. WHY it causes problems: the UI renders items in array order from the API response; customers see line items in a confusing reverse sequence and raise a production incident. Fix: use `opts => opts.WithStrictOrdering()` for the specific collection property in the options lambda, or assert the collection separately with `BeInAscendingOrder(x => x.Sequence)` to make ordering intent explicit.

**Gotcha 4 — Testcontainers.NET `WaitStrategy.UntilHttpRequestIsSucceeded` treats any non-5xx response (including 404 and 401) as "ready" — if the health endpoint requires an auth header, a 401 response will satisfy the wait strategy and the container will be considered started before it is actually accessible [community]** — A team configures `.WithWaitStrategy(Wait.ForUnixContainer().UntilHttpRequestIsSucceeded(r => r.ForPath("/health")))` on an API container that requires a `Bearer` token on all endpoints, including `/health`. The container starts, the unauthenticated request returns `401 Unauthorized`, and Testcontainers considers the container ready. The first test immediately issues a real authenticated request and occasionally encounters a race condition where the container's ASP.NET Core pipeline is not fully initialised. WHY it causes problems: the test suite passes ~90% of the time (the 401 response happens to arrive late enough that startup is complete) but fails 10% of the time with connection errors, producing a flaky suite that erodes team confidence. Fix: configure the health endpoint to return 200 without authentication, or use `.UntilMessageIsLogged("Application started")` as the wait strategy instead of an HTTP probe.

**Gotcha 5 — AutoFixture `[Frozen]` attribute applies in parameter declaration order — if a `[Frozen]` mock parameter appears *after* the SUT in a `[AutoMoqData]` theory signature, the SUT is constructed before the mock is frozen and receives a different untracked instance rather than the frozen one [community]** — A developer writes `public void Test([Frozen] Mock<IRepo> repo, MyService sut)` and wonders why `repo.Object` calls on the SUT never match the `Setup` configured on `repo`. The SUT was created before `repo` was frozen, so AutoFixture injected a freshly-created `IRepo` substitute into the constructor, not the `repo.Object`. WHY it causes problems: the test never exercises the configured mock behaviour; assertions like `repo.Verify(r => r.FindAsync(...), Times.Once)` always fail because the SUT's internal `IRepo` reference is a different object entirely. Fix: always declare `[Frozen]` parameters *before* the SUT parameter in the method signature so AutoFixture freezes them before resolving the SUT's constructor dependencies.

---

### Anti-Patterns Quick Reference — Cycle 53 Additions

| Anti-Pattern | Why It's Harmful | What to Do Instead |
|---|---|---|
| `IAsyncLifetime.InitializeAsync` without try/finally cleanup | Partial startup failures orphan resources; DisposeAsync never runs on throw | Wrap startup steps in try/finally within InitializeAsync; dispose failed resources inline |
| `SetupSequence` without `Verify(Times.Exactly(n))` | Extra calls return default; over-retry bugs produce NullReferenceException pointing at wrong code | Always follow SetupSequence with a call-count Verify; use MockBehavior.Strict |
| `BeEquivalentTo` on ordered collections without `WithStrictOrdering()` | Reversed sort order passes assertion; ordering bugs ship to production | Use `WithStrictOrdering()` option or assert `BeInAscendingOrder` separately |
| `UntilHttpRequestIsSucceeded` on auth-required health endpoints | 401 satisfies the wait strategy; container declared ready before fully initialised | Make health endpoint auth-exempt or use `UntilMessageIsLogged` instead |
| `[Frozen]` parameter declared after SUT in AutoFixture theory | SUT constructed before freeze; internal dependency is a different untracked instance | Always declare `[Frozen]` parameters before the SUT in theory method signatures |
| `[AutoData]` customization with overbroad type overrides | Domain-specific values silently applied to all T instances; boundary tests receive wrong data | Scope customizations narrowly; use `[InlineAutoData]` for boundary-sensitive cases |
